Where goods have been delivered to the consumer's home at the time of entry into the contract and, by its nature, the goods cannot be normally returned by post, the trader shall collect the goods at the trader's expense.

(3) In the case of any deterioration of the goods subject to return, the consumer is liable for the diminished value of the goods only in the case the consumer used the goods in a manner other than what is necessary to establish the nature, characteristics and functioning of the goods. In order to establish the nature, characteristics and functioning of the goods, the consumer should only handle and use the goods in the same manner as the consumer would customarily be allowed to do in a shop. The consumer shall not be liable for the diminished value of the goods in the case the trader has failed to draw the attention of the consumer to the existence of the right of withdrawal according to clauses 12 and 13 of subsection 1 of § 48 of this Act.

(3<sup>1</sup>) Where appropriate, the consumer also performs the obligations provided for in subsection 1 of § 62<sup>16</sup> of this Act.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

(4) If the consumer exercises the right of withdrawal after submission of the application specified in subsection 2 of § 48<sup>1</sup> of this Act, the consumer shall reimburse the trader for the value of what was delivered as the performance of the contract in proportion to what was delivered up to the time when the consumer withdrew from the contract, taking into consideration the total volume of the contract. The value of what was delivered is determined on the basis of the price agreed in the contract. If the contract price is unreasonably high, the value of what was delivered shall be calculated on the basis of the market value.

(5) In the case of a contract the object of which is the provision of a service, other continuous performance or sale of water, gas, electricity or heating through a network, the consumer is not obliged to reimburse the trader for the value of what was delivered during the withdrawal period if:

1\) the trader has failed to provide information to the consumer according to clauses 12, 13 or 15 of subsection 1 of § 48 of this Act; or

2\) the consumer has not expressly applied for the commencement of the provision of a service, other continuous performance or sale of water, gas, electricity of heating through a network pursuant to subsection 2 of § 48<sup>1</sup> of this Act during the withdrawal period.

(6) In the case of the contract the object of which is the delivery of digital content, the consumer is not obliged to reimburse the trader for the value of such digital content delivered to the consumer during the withdrawal period which was not delivered on a tangible medium if:

1\) the consumer has not given a prior express consent for the commencement of the delivery of the digital content before the end of the 14-day period provided for in subsection 1 of § 49 of this Act;

2\) the consumer has not acknowledged that the consumer loses the right of withdrawal when giving such consent; or

3\) the trader has failed to provide confirmation specified in subsection 1 of § 48<sup>1</sup> of this Act.

(7) The claims of the trader arising from withdrawal against the consumer are limited to that provided in this section and subsection 2 of § 49<sup>2</sup>.

(8) Contract terms which impede the right of withdrawal from being exercised, in particular agreements pursuant to which withdrawal is bound to payment of earnest money or a contractual penalty, are void.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 49<sup>4</sup>. Effect of withdrawal to collateral contract

(1) If the consumer exercises the right of withdrawal provided for in § 49 of this Act with respect to an off-premises contract, the consumer shall be deemed to have withdrawn from the collateral contract linked to the off-premises contract which the consumer has entered into with the trader or a third person on the basis of an agreement between the third person and the trader.

(2) If the consumer is deemed to have withdrawn from a collateral contract in the case specified in subsection 1 of this section, the trader or the third person may not require payment for other costs besides those provided for in subsection 2 of § 49<sup>2</sup> and § 49<sup>3</sup> of this Act.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 49<sup>5</sup>. Effect of withdrawal on consumer credit contract

(1) If an off-premises contract is a contract economically linked to a consumer credit contract for the purposes of § 414 of this Act, a consumer is deemed to have also withdrawn, in the case of withdrawal from an off-premises contract under the conditions provided for in § 49 of this Act, from the consumer credit contract and collateral contracts linked thereto for the purposes of subsection 3<sup>2</sup> of § 409 of this Act.

(2) In the case specified in subsection 1 of this section, a consumer shall not be required to pay interest or other expenses in the case of withdrawal from a consumer credit contract. The provisions of §§ 188–192 of this Act apply to other consequences of withdrawal.

(3) If credit is provided by a third party and the amount of the credit has already been paid to the trader, the rights and obligations of the trader with regard to the consumer transfer to the creditor in the case of withdrawal by the consumer.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 50. Prohibition on violation of provisions

A person or body provided by law may, pursuant to the procedure provided by law, require a trader who has violated the provisions of this Subchapter to terminate such violation and refrain from future violations.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 51. Mandatory nature of provisions

Agreements which derogate from the provisions of this Subchapter to the detriment of the consumer are void.

#### Subchapter 4 — Distance Contracts

\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 - entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 52. Definition of distance contract

(1) A contract between the trader and the consumer is deemed to be a distance contract if:\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

1\) the contract is entered into under a marketing or service-provision scheme used for the entry into of such contracts;\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

2\) \[Repealed – RT I, 04.02.2011, 1 – entry into force 05.04.2011\]

3\) the trader and the consumer are not present simultaneously at the same time upon entry into the contract; and\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

4\) contracting parties' declarations of intention for entry into the contract, including consumer's declaration of intention to assume the contractual obligations (hereinafter *order*), shall be sent exclusively by means of distance communication.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(2) Any method which enables a consumer and a trader who are not in the same place at the same time to organise the exchange of information necessary for negotiations and entry into a contract, in particular the use of telephone, radio, computer, facsimile or television or the delivery of addressed or unaddressed printed matter, including a catalogue or a standard letter, to a consumer, or press advertising with an order form, is deemed to be use of a means of distance communication.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(3) For the purposes of this Subchapter, investment, credit, insurance, banking and payment services are deemed to be financial services.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

##### § 53. Application of provisions

(1) \[Repealed – RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

(1<sup>1</sup>) In the case of such contracts of financial services which comprise an initial financial service agreement followed by successive operations or operations of the same nature linked in time, the provisions of this Subchapter and subsections 1 and 2 of § 28<sup>1</sup> apply only with regard to the initial contract. In the case there is no initial financial service agreement but successive operations or separate operations of the same nature linked in time are performed by the same contracting parties, the requirements concerning provision of information to consumers provided in §§ 54<sup>1</sup> and 55<sup>1</sup> of this Act apply only to the first operation. Where no operation of the same nature is performed for more than one year, the next operation is deemed to be the first of a new series of operations and therefore the provisions of §§ 54<sup>1</sup> and 55<sup>1</sup> of this Act apply.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(1<sup>2</sup>) The provisions of this Subchapter apply to distance contracts in the case of which the consumer pays or undertakes to pay a fee. The provisions of this Subchapter also apply in the case a trader supplies digital content to a consumer or provides a digital service to a consumer or undertakes to do so and the consumer provides or undertakes to provide personal data to the trader. This does not apply in the case the trader processes the personal data provided by the consumer solely for the purpose of supplying the digital content or a digital service or in order to comply with the requirements applicable to him under the legislation and does not process these data for any other purposes.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

(2) The provisions of this Subchapter do not apply to contracts which are entered into:

1\) for provision of social services;

2\) for provision of health services;

3\) for participation in gambling;

4\) for provision of transport services for passengers;

5\) for transfer or encumbering of an immovable with real rights or disposal of real rights relating to an immovable;

6\) for construction of new buildings or substantial conversion of buildings;

7\) for lease of dwellings;

8\) by means of notarial authentication;

9\) with regard to foodstuffs, beverages or other goods intended for everyday consumption which are delivered during frequent and regular tours of a trader to the residence, seat or workplace of the consumer;

10\) by means of automatic vending machines or automated commercial premises;

11\) with a provider of electronic communications services by means of a public telephone for the use thereof or for the use of one single connection by telephone, Internet or fax established by a consumer.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(3) \[Repealed – RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(4) The right of withdrawal provided for in subsection 1 of § 56 of this Act shall not apply to contracts the object of which is:\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

1\) the provision of a service or other continuous performance, where the contractual obligations of the trader arising from the contract are fully performed and the consumer pays a fee to the trader, only where the provision of the service or other performance has begun with the consumer's express prior consent and acknowledgement that the consumer is aware of losing their right to withdraw upon full performance of the contract by the trader;\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

1<sup>1</sup>) the delivery of the goods, provision of services or other performance which price is dependent of fluctuations in the financial market which cannot be controlled by the trader and which may occur within the withdrawal period, including to contracts the object of which is the services related to foreign currency or the securities specified in § 2 of the Securities Market Act;\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

2\) delivery of goods manufactured taking into account the personal needs of the consumer who is a party to the contract;\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

3\) for delivery of goods manufactured according to the conditions established by the consumer;\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

4\) the delivery of such goods which deteriorate or expire rapidly;\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

4<sup>1</sup>) the delivery of such goods in sealed packaging which are not suitable for return due to health protection or hygiene reasons and were unsealed after delivery;\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

4<sup>2</sup>) the delivery of such goods which are, after delivery, according to their nature, inseparably mixed with other items;\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

4<sup>3</sup>) the delivery of such alcoholic beverages, the price of which has been agreed upon at the time of the entry into the contract of sale, the delivery of which takes place after more than 30 days and the actual value of which is dependent on fluctuations in the market which cannot be controlled by the trader;\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

4<sup>4</sup>) the carrying out of urgent repairs or maintenance where the consumer has requested a visit from the trader for such purpose;\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

5\) the delivery of newspapers, magazines or periodicals with the exception of subscription contracts for an indefinite period for such publications;\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

6\) \[Repealed – RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

7\) the delivery of sealed audio or video recordings or computer software if the consumer has opened the package;\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

7<sup>1</sup>) the delivery for a fee of such digital content which is not delivered on a physical medium where the delivery thereof has begun with the consumer's prior express consent before the expiry of the withdrawal period and with the consumer’s acknowledgement that they are aware of the loss of their right of withdrawal, and the trader has given the confirmation specified in subsections 1 and 2 of § 55 of this Act;\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

7<sup>2</sup>) the provision of accommodation services, transportation of movables, use of motor vehicles, catering or services related to leisure activities if the trader undertakes to provide the services for a specific date or during a certain period upon conclusion of the above specified contract;\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

8\) at auctions where the consumer is present or the consumer has been granted an opportunity to be present;\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

9\) for travel and baggage insurance or other similar short-term insurance contracts entered into for a term of less than one month;

10\) provision of financial services which have been performed by both parties to the contract at an express request of the consumer before the consumer exercises their right of withdrawal.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

(4<sup>1</sup>) The provisions of § 55 of this Act do not apply to a distance financial service contract.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(5) Where a distance contract also complies with the provisions of a contract entered into between another consumer and a trader, the provisions of this Subchapter apply together with the special rules provided for this other type of contract. In the case of a distance financial service contract, the provisions of this Subchapter concerning the provision of pre-contractual information, the consumer's right of withdrawal and the consequences of exercising it, and the obligation of the trader to provide adequate explanations do not apply to funded pensions or in the case the European Union law or the rules transposing it provide otherwise for the provision of certain types of financial services.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(6) \[Repealed – RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(7) The exception provided for in clause 4<sup>4</sup> of subsection 4 of this section shall not extent to such a contract which is entered into on the occasion of such visit in addition to those ordered by the consumer, *inter alia* to a contract by which goods are delivered other than replacement parts necessary for making the repairs or carrying out the maintenance.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 54. Precontractual information to consumer

\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(1) Prior to entry into a contract or making a binding offer by a consumer for this purpose, a trader shall provide the consumer with the following information in a clear and comprehensible manner:

1\) data which enable the identification of the trader, in particular the trader's business name;

2\) the address of the place of business of the trader, their telephone number and email address, and where the trader provides other means of online communication which ensure that the consumer has the opportunity to maintain correspondence with the trader on a durable medium, including the date and time of such correspondence, and the details of those means, and where appropriate, the name and address of the place of business of the trader on whose behalf they act;\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

3\) the address of the place of business of the trader where the consumer can address complaints, if different from the address specified in accordance with clause 2 of this subsection;

4\) the main characteristics of the object of contract to the extent appropriate to the object of contract and the manner of presentation of information;

5\) in the case of digital content, the method of use thereof, the technical protective measures applied to it and compatibility thereof with any hardware and software what the trader knows of needs to know;\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

6\) the total price of the object of contract inclusive of taxes, or where the nature of the object of the contract is such that the price cannot reasonably be calculated in advance, the manner in which the price is to be calculated, and all additional freight, postal, delivery or any other costs, if the consumer has to cover these costs or where those costs cannot reasonably be calculated in advance, information on that such additional costs may be payable;

6<sup>1</sup>) where appropriate, information about that the price was adjusted on a personal basis in accordance with a decision based on automated processing;\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

7\) the charge for use of the means of distance communication used for entry into the contract, except in the case such charge corresponds to the normal charge for the use of such means of distance communication;

8\) when a consumer has to pay a sum of money as security or provide other financial security, the fact that this has to be done at the request of the trader, and the terms and conditions of such security;

9\) the arrangements for payment, delivery and execution of an order and the time by which the goods are delivered, the service is provided or other acts are performed;

10\) the minimum duration of the consumer's obligations under the contract, if it exists;

11\) in the case of long-term contracts the duration of the contract, or if the contract is of indeterminate duration or is to be extended automatically, the conditions for terminating the contract;

12\) where a right of withdrawal exists, the conditions, time limit and procedures for exercising that right in accordance with subsection 2<sup>2</sup> of § 56 of this Act;

13\) where a right of withdrawal exists, a standard form of application for withdrawal;

13<sup>1</sup>) where a right of withdrawal exists, in the case of a contract entered into through an online user interface, information concerning the existence and location of the withdrawal button or similar function provided in § 56<sup>4</sup> of this Act;\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

14\) the fact that if the consumer withdraws from the contract, the consumer shall bear the costs of returning the goods that constituted the object of the contract, and in the situation where the goods constituting the object of contract by their nature cannot be returned by normal post, the costs of removing the object, if the consumer has to bear these costs;\
\[RT I, 11.03.2016, 1 – entry into force 21.03.2016\]

15\) the fact that if the consumer exercises the right to withdraw from the contract after submitting the application specified in subsection 3 of § 55 of this Act, the consumer is obliged to compensate the trader for any reasonable costs according to subsection 5 of § 56<sup>2</sup> of this Act;

16\) where a right of withdrawal is not prescribed according to subsection 4 of § 53 of this Act, the information that the consumer has no right of withdrawal or, if the consumer may lose the right of withdrawal, information about the circumstances under which the right of withdrawal will be lost;

17\) upon offer of the maintenance service of the object of contract or customer service after the performance of the contract, the existence and the terms and conditions thereof;

18\) a reminder that the consumer can rely, upon non-compliance of an immovable, digital content and digital service with the terms and conditions of the contract, on the legal remedies provided by law;\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

19\) upon grant of additional warranty in addition to the legal remedies provided by law, the existence and terms and conditions thereof;

20\) the existence of a code of conduct observed by the trader, if the activities of the trader are based on it, and information on how to obtain a copy thereof;

21\) the procedure for handling complaints implemented by the trader, if it exists;

22\) the information on the possibilities of the consumer to have recourse to a body settling extra-judicial complaints and disputes and the terms and conditions of recourse.

(2) The information specified in subsection 1 of this section shall be provided or made available to the consumer to the means of distance communication used in an appropriate way and in plain and intelligible language. In so far as that information is provided on a durable medium, it shall be provided in a legible manner.

(2<sup>1</sup>) The means of communication provided by the trader and specified in clause 2 of subsection 1 of this section must enable the consumer to contact the trader quickly and communicate with them effectively.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

(3) The information specified in clauses 12, 14 and 15 of subsection 1 of this section may be also provided to the consumer by means of using the model instructions on withdrawal specified in subsection 4 of this section. If the trader provides the consumer with the model instructions on withdrawal, that information shall be deemed submitted to the consumer. That information is deemed submitted to the consumer only in the case the trader has properly completed the model instructions on withdrawal from the contract.

(4) The model instructions on withdrawal from contract shall be established by a regulation of the minister in charge of the policy sector.

(5) Where a distance contract is entered into by means of distance communication which allows limited space or time to display information, at least the information provided for in clauses 1, 4, 6, 11 and 12 of subsection 1 of this section is provided to the consumer prior to entry into such contract in the respective means of communication or by means thereof. Other information specified in subsection 1 of this section, including standard withdrawal form, is provided to the consumer in an appropriate manner according to subsection 2 of this section.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

(6) If the trader contacts the consumer by phone for the purpose of entry into a contract, the trader must inform the consumer, at the beginning of the telephone call, of the trader's name, and where appropriate, the name of the person on whose behalf the call is made, and the business purpose of the call.\
\[RT I, 11.03.2016, 1 – entry into force 21.03.2016\]

(7) In the case of a contract of indeterminate duration or a long-term contract the objects of which are continuing or recurring orders, the total price specified in clause 6 of subsection 1 of this section shall include the total costs per settlement period. Where such contracts are charged at a fixed rate, the total price shall also mean the total monthly costs. Where the total costs cannot be calculated in advance by reasonable efforts, the manner in which the price is to be calculated shall be provided.

(8) If the trader failed to inform the consumer of the obligation to pay the costs specified in clauses 6 or 14 of subsection 1 of this section, the consumer shall not bear these costs.

(9) The provisions on the obligation to provide precontractual information specified in subsection 2 of § 14 and § 14<sup>1</sup> of this Act shall not apply to preparations for entry into a distance contract.

(10) The trader shall prove compliance with the obligation to provide precontractual information provided for in this section.

(11) The information provided as precontractual information shall form a part of the contract, unless the parties have expressly agreed otherwise\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 54<sup>1</sup>. Precontractual information to consumer in case of financial service contract

\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(1) Within a reasonable period of time before the entry into a distance financial service contract or the making of a binding offer by the consumer on a durable medium, the trader provides the consumer with the following information in a clear and comprehensible manner, in an easily legible form, by selecting a typeface and font size which makes this information noticeable and comprehensible in the ordinary course of attention:\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

1\) the data enabling identification of the trader, its area of activity and, where applicable, the same information concerning the trader on whose behalf the trader operates;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

1<sup>1</sup>) the address of the place of business of the trader and any other address important in the relationship between the consumer and the trader, as well as the telephone number and email address of the trader or details of other means of communication offered by the trader which enable the consumer to contact the trader quickly and communicate with them effectively and ensure that the consumer is able to store this correspondence on a durable medium, where appropriate providing the same information concerning the trader on whose behalf the trader is acting;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

1<sup>2</sup>) the contact details of the trader which enable the consumer to submit complaints to the trader and, where applicable, to the trader on whose behalf the trader acts;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

2\) \[repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

3\) \[repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

4\) the commercial register number or registry code in the case the trader is entered in the commercial register or an equivalent public register, as well as the name of the register;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

5\) where an authorisation is required for the activities of the trader, the name, address, website address and other contact details of the oversight authority;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

6\) the main characteristics of the financial service;

7\) the total price of the financial service that the consumer pays to the trader, including all fees, taxes and expenses related to the financial service and all taxes paid through the trader, or, where the exact price cannot be indicated, the basis for the calculation of the price that allows the consumer to verify the price;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

7<sup>1</sup>) where applicable, information on the consequences of late payment or failure to make the payment;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

7<sup>2</sup>) where applicable, information that the price has been individually adjusted on the basis of a decision based on automated processing;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

8\) additional costs arising from the use of a means of communication and other possible taxes and costs which are not included in the price and which are not paid through the trader;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 - entry into force 01.09.2026\]

9\) the procedure for payment for the financial service and circumstances relating to the provision of the financial service and performance of the contract;

9<sup>1</sup>) where environmental or social factors are integrated into the investment strategy of the financial service, information on the environmental or social objectives pursued by the financial service;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

10\) special risks associated with the financial service due to the peculiarity of financial instruments or financial operations or the dependence of the price of financial services on financial markets over which the trader has no influence and the fact that the performance of previous periods does not guarantee the performance of subsequent periods;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

11\) the minimum term of the contract if the financial service is provided continuously or recurrently during a specific term;

12\) indication of the existence or absence of a right of withdrawal in the financial service contract and, where the right of withdrawal exists, information on the conditions for exercising the right of withdrawal, including the withdrawal period, as well as the amount of money that the consumer may be required to pay and the consequences of not exercising the right of withdrawal;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

13\) the right of the parties to cancel the contract or withdraw from the contract and the contractual penalties imposed in such cases;

13<sup>1</sup>) practical instructions and rules for exercising the right of withdrawal provided in § 56 of this Act, including the telephone number and email address of the trader or details of other relevant means of communication to which the notice of withdrawal is to be sent;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

13<sup>2</sup>) where a right of withdrawal exists, in the case of a contract entered into via an online user interface, information concerning the existence and location of the withdrawal button or similar function provided in § 56<sup>4</sup> of this Act;\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

14\) \[repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

15\) agreements on law and jurisdiction applicable to the contract;

16\) in which language the contract conditions and the information provided prior to the entry into the contract are submitted and in which language the trader undertakes, with the agreement of the consumer, to forward the information during the term of the financial service contract entered into by this means of communication;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

17\) information on the possibilities of the consumer to have recourse to a body settling extra-judicial complaints and disputes and the terms and conditions of recourse;

18\) information on the procedure for compensation for damage not regulated by the Guarantee Fund Act;

19\) possible restrictions concerning the period of validity of the information submitted in accordance with this subsection.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(2) \[Repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(3) In the case of voice telephony communications, the name of the trader and the commercial purpose of the call must be clearly communicated to the consumer at the beginning of the conversation. Where a phone call is or may be recorded, the consumer is notified thereof.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(4) \[Repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(5) In the case the financial service is offered by communication by telephone, subject to the explicit consent of the consumer only the following information may be given:

1\) the data enabling the identification of the identity and area of activity of the trader and, where appropriate, data enabling the identification of the identity of the trader on whose behalf the trader operates and its area of activity;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

2\) the main characteristics of the financial service;

3\) the price to be paid by the consumer to the trader for the financial service, including all taxes paid through the trader or, where the exact price cannot be indicated, the basis for the calculation of the price, which allows the consumer to verify the price;\
\[RT I, 27,05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

4\) reference to possible taxes and costs that are not included in the price and not paid via the provider of the financial service;

5\) an indication of the existence or absence of a right of withdrawal in the financial service contract and, where a right of withdrawal exists, information on the right of withdrawal and the conditions for exercising it, including the amount that the consumer may be required to pay and the consequences of not exercising that right.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(6) \[Repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(7) \[Repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(8) In the case provided in subsection 5 of this section, the trader informs the consumer of the availability of the other information specified in subsection 1 and describes the nature of this information.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(9) In the case of a distance contract for the provision of a payment service, the provisions of clauses 8–10, 12, 13<sup>1</sup>, 18 and 19 of subsection 1 of this section and subsection 1 of § 711 and subsection 1 of § 711<sup>1</sup> of this Act apply.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(10) The provisions on the obligation to provide pre-contractual information specified in subsection 2 of § 14 and §§ 14<sup>1</sup> and 54 of this Act shall not apply to the obligation to provide pre-contractual information specified in this section.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(11) The trader demonstrates the provision of pre-contractual information provided in this Subchapter.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

##### § 54<sup>2</sup>. Entry into contract by telephone

(1) If the parties enter into a contract by telephone, the consumer is bound by the obligations assumed by telephone only in the case the trader has confirmed what was communicated by phone on a durable medium and the consumer has confirmed the intention to be bound by the obligation assumed by telephone in a format which can be reproduced in writing. Upon violation of the requirements specified in this section, the goods, services or other performance delivered by the trader to the consumer shall be deemed to be unsolicited goods, services or other performance for the purpose of subsection 1 of § 99 of this Act.

(2) \[Repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(3) The provisions of this section shall not apply in the case the contract is entered into on the initiative of the consumer.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 54<sup>3</sup>. Notification requirements for contracts entered into through online marketplace

(1) An online marketplace is a trading venue where a consumer can enter into contracts with other traders or consumers by means of communication devices using software, including websites, parts of websites or applications operated by the trader or on behalf of the trader.

(2) An online marketplace operator is a trader that provides consumers with an online marketplace.

(3) An online marketplace operator provides the consumer with the following information before entry into a distance contract through that place or making a binding offer by the consumer in a clear and understandable manner and in a manner suitable for the means of communication:

1\) general information made available in a specific part of the web interface and which is directly and easily accessible from the website on which the offers are presented and which concerns the main parameters which determine the ranking of offers submitted to consumers as a result of the search, as defined in clause 8 of subsection 1 of § 2 of the Consumer Protection Act, and the relative importance of these parameters compared to other parameters;

2\) information on whether or not a third party offering things, services, digital content or other benefits on an online marketplace is a trader or not, based on a third party's statement to the an online marketplace operator;

3\) where a third party that provides things, services, digital content or other benefits is not a trader, information about that the contract is not subject to the consumer rights arising from the European Union consumer protection law;

4\) where appropriate, information on how the obligations related to the contract are distributed between a third party providing things, services, digital content or other benefits and the online marketplace operator.

(4) The information published pursuant to clause 4 of subsection 3 of this section does not affect the liability of the online marketplace operator or third-party trader.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

##### § 55. Confirmation of information

(1) The trader shall provide the consumer with the confirmation of the contract entered into, on a durable medium within a reasonable time after the entry into the contract but not later than at the time of delivery of the goods or before the provision of the service or performance begins.

(2) The confirmation specified in subsection 1 of this section shall include the information specified in subsection 1 of § 54 of this Act unless the trader has already provided this information to the consumer on a durable medium prior to the entry into the contract, and if the object of contract is digital content, the trader's confirmation stating that the consumer has given an explicit consent and acknowledgement pursuant to clause 7<sup>1</sup> of subsection 4 of § 53 of this Act for the commencement of the delivery of the digital content.

(3) Where the consumer wants the provision, for a fee, of services or other continuous performance or sale of water, gas, electricity or heating through a network to begin during the withdrawal term prescribed in § 56 of this Act, the trader requires that the consumer makes an express statement in this regard, and an acknowledgement that when the trader has fully performed the contract, the consumer no longer has the right to withdraw.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

##### § 55<sup>1</sup>. Specifications for provision of information in case of financial service contract

(1) In addition to the provisions of subsection 1 of § 54<sup>1</sup> of this Act, the trader communicates to the consumer, within a reasonable period of time before the entry into the financial service contract or the making of an offer by the consumer, the contractual conditions and other relevant information provided by law on a durable medium. Upon request, this information is provided in a format suitable for and accessible by a disabled person, including a person with a visual disability.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(2) In the case described in subsection 8 of § 54<sup>1</sup> of this Act, the trader must perform the obligation provided for in subsection 1 of this section immediately after the conclusion of the financial service contract.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(2<sup>1</sup>) Where the information specified in subsection 1 of § 54<sup>1</sup> of this Act is submitted later than one day before the entry into the financial service contract or the making of a binding offer by the consumer, the trader sends a reminder to the consumer concerning the possibility to withdraw from the contract and the rules to be followed for withdrawal in accordance with § 56 of this Act. The reminder is provided to the consumer on a durable medium within one to seven days after the entry into the contract or the making of a binding declaration of intention by the consumer.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(2<sup>2</sup>) Where a means of communication technically limiting the number of characters displayed is used, the trader may submit the pre-contractual information listed in subsection 1 of § 54<sup>1</sup> of this Act in layers, except for the data listed in clauses 1, 6, 7, 8 and 12 of the same subsection. It must be possible to view, save and print all the information specified in this subsection as a single, complete document. The trader undertakes to provide all the above specified information to the consumer before entry into a distance financial service contract.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(3) \[Repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(4) \[Repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(5) \[Repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(6) Where the consumer wants the provision of financial services to begin during the withdrawal period prescribed in § 56 of this Act, the consumer shall provide express consent for it.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(7) If a unit-linked life insurance contract is entered into using such means of distance communication which do not enable providing of information during a reasonable period of time before the entry into the contract, the insurer shall communicate, with the consent of the policyholder, the assessment specified in clause 4<sup>3</sup> of subsection 2 of § 428 of this Act immediately after the entry into the insurance contract provided that the insurer has previously offered the policyholder an opportunity to postpone the entry into the insurance contract until receipt of the assessment.\
\[RT I, 17.11.2017, 3 – entry into force 01.10.2018\]

(8) The provisions of subsection 7 of this Act shall apply to the assessment specified in clause 2 of subsection 2 of § 192 and clause 5 of subsection 2 of § 198 of the Insurance Activities Act if such means of distance communication are used upon entry into a unit-linked life insurance contract through an insurance broker and insurance agent which do not enable providing of information to the customer during a reasonable period of time before the entry into the contract.\
\[RT I, 17.11.2017, 3 – entry into force 01.10.2018\]

##### § 55<sup>2</sup>. Providing explanations to consumer

(1) Before entry into a distance financial service contract, the trader provides the consumer with explanations free of charge in order to enable the consumer to assess whether the contract and additional services offered are suitable for their needs and financial situation, including explaining to the consumer:

1\) pre-contractual information in accordance with subsection 1 of § 54<sup>1</sup> of this Act;

2\) main characteristics of the financial service contract offered, including possible additional services;

3\) consequences for the consumer arising from the financial service contract, including, where applicable, the consequences of the consumer's failure to comply with a payment obligation or late payment.

(2) Where the trader only uses online means of communication with the consumer, the consumer has the right to request human intervention. The trader ensures human intervention before the entry into the distance financial service contract and, in justified cases, after the entry into the financial service contract and in the same language that was used for the provision of pre-contractual information in accordance with subsection 1 of § 54<sup>1</sup> of this Act.

(3) The trader demonstrates compliance with the obligation to provide adequate explanations provided in this section, including ensuring human intervention.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

##### § 56. Right of withdrawal from contract

(1) A consumer may withdraw from a distance contract within 14 days without giving any reason.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(1<sup>1</sup>) In the case of a contract the object of which is the delivery of goods, the period specified in subsection 1 of this section shall commence as of the day when the consumer or a third person other than the carrier and indicated by the consumer acquires physical possession of the goods, or:

1\) where several goods that are delivered separately have to be delivered to the consumer pursuant to the contract, as of the day when the consumer or a third person other than the carrier and indicated by the consumer acquires physical possession of the goods;

2\) where the goods have to be delivered to the consumer in multiple lots or pieces, as of the day when the consumer or a third person other than the carrier and indicated by the consumer acquires the physical possession of the last lot or piece;

3\) in the case of a long-term contract the object of which is repeated delivery of goods during a defined period of time, as of the day when the consumer or a third person who is not a carrier and indicated by the consumer acquires physical possession of the first good delivered.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(1<sup>2</sup>) In the case of a contract the object of which is the provision of a service or other continuous performance, the period indicated in subsection 1 of this section shall commence as of the day of entry into the contract.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(1<sup>3</sup>) In the case of sale of water, gas, electricity or heating through a network and in the case of digital content which cannot be delivered on a tangible medium, the period specified in subsection 1 of this section shall commence as of the day of entry into the contract.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(1<sup>4</sup>) In the case of a contract for provision of financial services, the term for withdrawal shall begin from the day of the entry into the contract or from the performance of the obligation provided for in subsection 1 of § 54<sup>1</sup> and subsections 1 and 2 of § 55<sup>1</sup> of this Act if this takes place after entry into the contract.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(1<sup>5</sup>) The consumer may withdraw from a distance contract for life insurance or pension insurance within 30 days as of the date on which the consumer is informed of entry into the contract or performance of the obligation provided for in subsection 1 of § 54<sup>1</sup> and subsections 1 and 2 of § 55<sup>1</sup> of this Act if this takes place after entry into the contract.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(1<sup>6</sup>) If the trader has violated the obligation to provide information specified in clause 12 of subsection 1 of § 54 of this Act, the withdrawal period shall expire 12 months after the expiry of the expiry of the withdrawal period determined in the manner provided for in subsections 1<sup>1</sup>–1<sup>3</sup> of this section. If the trader delayed the provision of the information on the right of withdrawal specified in the preceding sentence to the consumer but still provided it within 12 months as of the day referred to in subsections 1<sup>1</sup>–1<sup>3</sup> of this section, the withdrawal period shall expire 14 days after the receipt of the information.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(2) Where a distance contract is a financial service contract and the consumer has not received the contract conditions or the information specified in §§ 54<sup>1</sup> and 55<sup>1</sup> of this Act, the withdrawal period expires in any case 12 months and 14 days after the entry into the distance contract. This does not apply where the consumer was not informed of their right of withdrawal and the conditions for exercising it.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(2<sup>1</sup>) The deadline for withdrawal from a distance contract shall be deemed to have been observed by the consumer if the consumer has dispatched a notification concerning the withdrawal to the trader during the withdrawal period.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(2<sup>2</sup>) The consumer may withdraw from a contract by means of a standard form of application for withdrawal or by presenting another unequivocal application for withdrawal. The provisions of this section shall not apply to withdrawal from the contract for provision of a financial service.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(2<sup>3</sup>) The standard form of application for withdrawal shall be established by a regulation of the minister in charge of the policy sector.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(2<sup>4</sup>) If the consumer uses the website of the trader for sending the application for withdrawal, the trader shall immediately send a confirmation to the consumer on a durable medium concerning the receipt of the application for withdrawal.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(2<sup>5</sup>) The consumer shall prove withdrawal from the contract in compliance with the provisions of this section.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(3) \[Repealed – RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(4) \[Repealed – RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(5) \[Repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

##### § 56<sup>1</sup>. Trader's obligations upon consumer's withdrawal

(1) Upon receipt of an application for withdrawal, the trader shall return to the consumer immediately but at not later than after 14 days all the payments received from the consumer based on the contract, *inter alia* the costs of delivery of the goods borne by the consumer.

(2) Where a consumer withdraws from a contract for the provision of financial services, the provider of the financial service shall reimburse the consumer, immediately upon receipt of the application for withdrawal but not later than 30 days after it, for all payments received from the consumer under the contract.

(3) If the consumer has expressly opted for a type of delivery other than the least expensive type of standard delivery offered by the trader, the trader shall not be required to reimburse the consumer for the costs which exceed the costs relating to the type of standard delivery.

(4) The trader shall carry out the reimbursements specified in subsections 1 and 2 of this section using the same means of payment as was used by the consumer for making the payments, unless the consumer has expressly agreed on the use of other means of payment and provided that the consumer does not incur any service charges or other costs as a result of such reimbursement.

(5) If the object of contract is the delivery of goods, the trader may refuse to make the reimbursements specified in subsections 1 and 2 of this section on the basis of § 111 of this Act until the consumer has returned the goods constituting the object of contract to the trader or until the consumer has supplied evidence of having sent the goods back. The trader shall not have the right specified in this section in the case the trader has agreed to collect the goods constituting the object of contract.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(6) Where appropriate, the trader also performs the obligations provided for in subsections 2–5 of § 62<sup>15</sup> of this Act.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

##### § 56<sup>2</sup>. Consumer's obligations upon withdrawal

(1) If goods were delivered to the consumer as an object of contract, the consumer shall return the goods to the trader immediately but not later than after 14 days as of making an application for withdrawal or deliver the goods to the trader or a person indicated by the trader. The consumer shall not have the obligation to return the goods specified in the first sentence of this subsection in the case the trader has agreed to collect the goods. The consumer shall be deemed to have performed the obligation to return the goods in due time if the consumer returns the goods constituting the object of contract during the period specified in the first sentence of this subsection.

(2) Where a consumer withdraws from a distance financial service contract, they return to the trader the money and other property objects received without delay, but not later than within 30 days after making the application for withdrawal.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(3) The consumer shall bear the direct costs relating to the return of the goods delivered to the consumer as the object of contract, unless the parties have agreed otherwise. The consumer shall have no obligation to bear the costs if the trader has failed to inform the consumer of the fact that the consumer has to bear these costs.

(4) In the case of any deterioration of the goods subject to return, the consumer is liable for the diminished value of the goods only in the case the consumer used the goods in a manner other than what is necessary to establish the nature, characteristics and functioning of the goods. In order to establish the nature, characteristics and functioning of the goods, the consumer should only handle and use the goods in the same manner as the consumer would customarily be allowed to do in a shop. The consumer shall not be liable for the diminished value of the goods in the case the trader has failed to draw the attention of the consumer to the existence of the right of withdrawal according to clauses 12 and 13 of subsection 1 of § 54 of this Act.

(4<sup>1</sup>) Where appropriate, the consumer also performs the obligations provided for in subsection 1 of § 62<sup>16</sup> of this Act.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 28.05.2022\]

(5) Where the consumer exercises the right of withdrawal after submission of the application specified in subsection 3 of § 55 of this Act, the consumer compensates the trader for the value delivered as performance of the contract in proportion to the value delivered until the time when the consumer withdrew from the contract, taking into account the total volume of the contract. The value of the transfer is determined on the basis of the total price agreed in the contract. Where the contract price is unreasonably high, the value of the transfer is calculated on the basis of the market price.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(5<sup>1</sup>) Where the consumer withdraws from a distance financial service contract after the submission of the application specified in subsection 6 of § 55<sup>1</sup> of this Act, the consumer pays the trader for the services provided in accordance with the contract, but in an amount not exceeding what is proportionate to the share of the service already provided out of the total volume of the contract The amount payable must not be of such magnitude that it could be construed as a contractual penalty.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

(6) In the case of a contract the object of which is the provision of a service, other continuous performance or sale of water, gas, electricity or heating through a network, the consumer is not obliged to reimburse the trader for the value of what was delivered during the withdrawal period if:

1\) the trader has failed to provide information to the consumer according to clause 12, 13 or 15 of subsection 1 of § 54 of this Act or in the case of a financial service according to clause 12 of subsection 1 of § 54<sup>1</sup> or this Act, or

2\) the consumer has not expressly applied for the commencement of the provision of a service, other continuous performance or sale of water, gas, electricity of heating through a network pursuant to subsection 3 of § 55 or subsection 6 of § 55<sup>1</sup> of this Act during the withdrawal period.

(7) In the case of the contract the object of which is the delivery of digital content, the consumer is not obliged to reimburse the trader for the value of such digital content delivered to the consumer during the withdrawal period which was not delivered on a tangible medium if:

1\) the consumer has not given a prior express consent for the commencement of the delivery of the digital content before the end of the 14-day period provided for in subsection 1 of § 56 of this Act;

2\) the consumer has not acknowledged that the consumer loses the right of withdrawal when giving such consent; or

3\) the business has failed to provide confirmation specified in subsections 1 and 2 of § 55 of this Act.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 01.01.2022\]

(8) The claims of the trader arising from withdrawal against the consumer are limited to that provided in this section and subsection 3 of § 56<sup>1</sup>.

(9) Contract terms which impede the right of withdrawal from being exercised, in particular agreements pursuant to which withdrawal is bound to payment of earnest money or a contractual penalty, are void.

(10) \[Repealed – RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

##### § 56<sup>3</sup>. Effect of withdrawal to collateral contract

(1) If the consumer exercises the right of withdrawal provided for in § 56 of this Act with respect to a distance contract, the consumer shall be deemed to have withdrawn from the collateral contract linked to the distance contract which the consumer has entered into with the trader or a third person on the basis of an agreement between the third person and the trader.

(2) If the consumer is deemed to have withdrawn from a collateral contract in the case specified in subsection 1 of this section, the trader or the third person may not require the consumer to bear other costs besides those provided for in subsection 3 of § 56<sup>1</sup> and § 56<sup>2</sup> of this Act.

(3) If a distance contract is a contract for the provision of a financial service which is linked to another distance contract for the provision of the service by the provider of the financial service or any third persons based on an agreement between them, the provisions of §§ 188–192 of this Act apply to the consequences of withdrawal instead of the provisions of subsection 2 of this section.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 56<sup>4</sup>. Exercise of right of withdrawal in case of contract entered into via online interface

(1) The trader also allows the consumer to withdraw from the contract entered into via an online interface by using the withdrawal button or a similar function. The back button or similar function must be highlighted and marked with the words "Withdraw from the contract" or other unambiguous and easily legible text.

(2) The withdrawal button or similar function must be permanently and easily accessible to the consumer throughout the withdrawal period. This must allow the consumer to submit an online withdrawal application where the following information can be easily entered or confirmed:

1\) the name of the consumer;

2\) detailed data to identify the contract from which the consumer wishes to withdraw;

3\) detailed data of the electronic means through which the confirmation of receipt of the withdrawal application is sent to the consumer.

(3) Where the consumer has filled in the withdrawal application specified in subsection 2 of this section, the trader must allow the consumer to send it to them by means of a confirmation button or a similar function. The confirmation button or similar function must be marked with the words “I confirm the withdrawal” or other such unambiguous and easily legible text.

(4) A trader must immediately confirm the receipt of a withdrawal application confirmed by means of a confirmation button or a similar function on a durable medium. The confirmation sent to the consumer must indicate the content of the withdrawal application and the date and time of transmission.

(5) The consumer is deemed to have withdrawn from the contract on time if they have sent an application therefor to the trader within the withdrawal period.\
\[RT I, 27.05.2026, 2 – entry into force 01.09.2026\]

##### § 57. Effect of withdrawal on consumer credit contract

\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(1) If a distance contract is a contract economically linked to a consumer credit contract for the purposes of § 414 of this Act, a consumer is deemed to have also withdrawn, in the case of withdrawal from the contract under the conditions provided for in § 56 of this Act, from the consumer credit contract and collateral contracts linked thereto for the purposes of subsection 409 (3<sup>2</sup>) of this Act.

(2) In the case provided for in subsection 1 of this section, the consumer shall not be required to pay interest or expenses. The provisions of §§ 188–192 of this Act apply to other consequences of withdrawal.

(3) If credit is granted by a third party and the amount of the credit has already been paid to the trader, the rights and obligations of the trader with regard to the consumer transfer to the creditor in the case of withdrawal by the consumer.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 57<sup>1</sup>. Withdrawal from contract linked to contract for provision of financial services

\[Repealed – RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 58. Consequences of withdrawal from contract for provision of financial services

\[Repealed – RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 59. Performance of contract

\[Repealed – RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 60. Restrictions on use of means of distance communication

An offer may be made to a consumer by automated calling systems without human intervention, fax, telephone answering machine or electronic mail only with the prior consent of the consumer. Other means of distance communication which allow individual communication may be used for communicating an offer only if the consumer has not expressly forbidden the use thereof.\
\[RT I, 04.02.2011, 1 – entry into force 05.04.2011\]

##### § 61. Prohibition on violation of provisions

A person or body provided by law may, pursuant to the procedure provided by law, require a trader who has violated the provisions of this Subchapter to terminate such violation and refrain from future violations.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 62. Mandatory nature of provisions

Agreements which derogate from the provisions of this Subchapter to the detriment of the consumer are void.

#### Subchapter 5 — Contracts Entered into through Computer Network

\[RT I 2004, 13, 86 - entry into force 15.04.2004\]

##### § 62<sup>1</sup>. Entry into contract through computer network

\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(1) The trader who enters into a contract through a computer network shall make available to the other contracting party suitable and efficient technical means which are accessible by the other party and by which the other party is able to identify and correct typing errors before transmitting the order.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(2) Before transmission of an order specified in subsection 1 of this section, the trader shall notify the other contracting party of:

1\) the technical stages involved in entering into the contract;

2\) whether the trader will preserve the text of the contract after entry into the contract and whether the text will remain available to the other contracting party;

3\) the technical means for identifying and correcting typing errors;

4\) the languages in which the contract may be entered into;

5\) the rules observed by the trader, and the electronic means for examining the rules.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(3) The trader shall immediately confirm in electronic form the receipt of an order.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(4) \[Repealed – RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(5) The terms of the contract, including the standard terms, shall be presented to the other contracting party in a manner which enables them to be saved and reproduced.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(6) The provisions of subsections 1–3 of this section do not apply if the contract is entered into by electronic mail or any other similar personal means of distance communication.

(7) \[Repealed – RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(8) The provisions of this section do not preclude or restrict any obligations of a trader to provide the other contracting party with any other information prescribed by law.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 62<sup>2</sup>. Additional requirements for entry into contract with consumer

(1) At the latest at the beginning of the ordering process, the trader shall provide the following information in a clear and legible manner:

1\) delivery restrictions, if any;

2\) acceptable means of payment.

(2) If a contract entered into through a computer network prescribes an obligation to pay, the trader shall make the consumer aware of the information provided for in clauses 4, 6, 10 and 11 of subsection 1 of § 54 of this Act in a clear and prominent manner in addition to the provisions of subsection 2 of § 62<sup>1</sup> of this Act immediately before the transmission of the order. In the case of failure to comply with the notification requirement, the consumer shall not be bound by the contract or order.

(3) The trader shall ensure that the consumer, when placing his order, explicitly acknowledges that the order implies an obligation to pay. If placing an order entails activating a button or a similar function, the button or similar function shall be labelled in an easily legible manner only with the words ‘order with obligation to pay’ or a corresponding unambiguous formulation indicating that placing the order entails an obligation to pay. If the trader has not complied with the requirements provided for in this subsection, the consumer shall not be bound by the contract or order.

(4) The provisions of this section shall not apply to contracts entered into through a computer network, the object of which is the provision of a financial service.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

##### § 62<sup>3</sup>. Mandatory nature of provisions

Agreements which derogate from the provisions of this Subchapter to the detriment of the consumer are void.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

#### Subchapter 6 — Contract for Supply of Digital Content and Digital Service

\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 - entry into force 01.01.2022\]

##### § 62<sup>4</sup>. Concept of contract for supply of digital content and digital service

(1) By a contract for supply of digital content or digital services, a trader supplies the digital content or a digital service to the consumer or undertakes to supply it and the consumer pays for it in cash or in digital representations of value or undertakes to do so.

(2) The provisions of this Subchapter also apply to contracts by which a trader supplies digital content or a digital service to a consumer or undertakes to do so and the consumer provides or undertakes to provide personal data to the trader. This does not apply in the case the trader processes the personal data provided by the consumer solely for the purpose of supplying digital content or a digital service or in order to comply with the requirements applicable to them under the legislation and does not process these data for any other purposes.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 01.01.2022\]

##### § 62<sup>5</sup>. Application of provisions

(1) The provisions of this Subchapter also apply in the case digital content or a digital service is developed in accordance with the description submitted by the consumer.

(2) The provisions of this Subchapter, except the provisions of §§ 62<sup>6</sup> and 62<sup> 13</sup>, also apply to a physical medium which serves only as a carrier of the digital content.

(3) The provisions of this Subchapter do not apply to digital content or digital services contained in or connected to a digital item specified in subsection 6 of § 208 of this Act.

(4) The provisions of this Subchapter do not apply to contracts the object of which is:

1\) provision of services other than digital services, regardless of whether the business uses digital forms or means to create the result of the service or to supply or transmit the result to the consumer;

2\) electronic communications services specified in clause 6 of § 2 of the Electronic Communications Act, except numberless interpersonal communication services defined in clause 34<sup>2</sup> of § 2 of the same Act;

3\) health care services;

4\) gambling services which involve wagering a stake with pecuniary value in games of chance, including games of chance with an element of skill, such as lotteries, casino games, poker and betting transactions, and which are provided by electronic means or by any other technological means facilitating communication at the individual request of the recipient of such services;

5\) financial services;

6\) software offered by a trader under a free and open source license, in the case the consumer does not pay in cash or in digital representations of value and the trader processes the personal data provided by the consumer solely for the purpose of improving the security, compatibility or interoperability of the specific software;

7\) supply of digital content made available to the public by means other than signal transmission as part of a performance or event, such as the digital presentation of cinematographic images;

8\) digital content provided by a holder of information specified in clauses 1 and 2 of subsection 1 of § 5 of the Public Information Act.

(5) If a contract concluded between the same trader and the same consumer includes elements of supply of digital content or a digital service and elements of supply of another service or item, the provisions of this Subchapter only apply to the elements of the contract concerning the digital content or digital service. The provisions of the first sentence do not affect the application of subsection 3 of this section.

(6) Section 62<sup>19</sup> of this Act does not apply in the case the package within the meaning of the Electronic Communications Act contains any elements of the internet connection service defined in clause 8<sup>4</sup> of § 2 or any elements of a number-based interpersonal service defined in clause 34<sup>1</sup> of § 2 of the same Act.

(7) Unless otherwise provided in this Subchapter, the provisions of the general part of this Act and which concern the type of contract to which the contract for the supply of digital content or a digital service conforms also apply to the contract for the supply of digital content and a digital service.

(8) Where the provisions of this Subchapter are in conflict with another European Union law regulating a certain sector or regulatory matter, this prevails over the provisions of this section.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 01.01.2022\]

##### § 62<sup>6</sup>. Supply of digital content and digital service

(1) Where a trader is required to supply digital content or a digital service to a consumer and the parties have not agreed otherwise, the trader shall supply the content or service immediately after entering into the contract.

(2) A trader has performed an obligation to supply or an obligation to provide a service if:

1\) the digital content or the means suitable for accessing or downloading the digital content have been made available or accessible to the consumer or to a physical or virtual system chosen by the consumer for that purpose;

2\) the digital service has been made accessible to the consumer or to a physical or virtual system chosen by the consumer for that purpose.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 01.01.2022\]

##### § 62<sup>7</sup>. Compliance of digital content and digital service with conditions of contract

(1) Digital content or a digital service must comply with the conditions of the contract.

(2) Digital content or a digital service is deemed to comply with the conditions of a contract, among other things, if:

1\) its description, quantity, quality, method of use, compatibility, interoperability and other characteristics comply with the agreed conditions;

2\) it is suitable for a certain special purpose for which the consumer needs it and of which the consumer has notified the trader not later than at the time of entry into the contract and which the trader has agreed to;

3\) it is supplied with all agreed accessories and instructions, including installation instructions and customer support; and

4\) agreed updates are made to it.

(3) In addition to the information specified in subsection 2 of this section, digital content or a digital service must:

1\) be suitable for the purpose for which this type of digital content or digital service is normally used, taking into account the law of the European Union and Estonia and technical standards or, in their absence, sectoral codes of conduct in force in a specific field of activity;

2\) be in the quantity and possess the qualities and performance features normally associated with the digital content and digital service of that type, including the usages, compatibility, accessibility, consistency and security that the consumer can reasonably expect, based on the nature of the content or service and taking into account public statements made by the trader itself or by others on its behalf or involved in earlier stages of the transaction chain about the content and services, in particular in advertising or on labelling;

3\) be handed over together with such accessories and instructions as the consumer may reasonably expect to receive;

4\) comply with a trial version or preview of the digital content or digital service made available by the trader before the entry into the contract;

5\) be updated in accordance with § 62<sup>8</sup> of this Act; and

6\) be in the latest version available at the time of entry into the contract, unless otherwise agreed.

(4) Statements specified in clause 2 of subsection 3 of this section is not binding on a trader if the trader certifies that:

1\) they did not know or should not have known of the statement in question;

2\) by the time of entry into the contract, the statement had been corrected in the same or comparable manner as it was made; or

3\) the statement could not affect the decision to acquire digital content or a digital service.

(5) The digital content or digital service does not comply with the conditions of the contract if its use pursuant to subsection 2 or 3 of this section is hindered or restricted by a restriction arising from infringement of the rights of any third parties, in particular intellectual property rights.

(6) Where a contract provides for the continuous supply of digital content or a digital service within a specified period of time, the content or service must comply with the conditions of the contract throughout that period.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 01.01.2022\]

##### § 62<sup>8</sup>. Obligation to update

(1) A trader must ensure that a consumer is informed of updates and that updates, including security updates, which are necessary to ensure the compliance of the digital content or digital service with the conditions of the contract, are provided to the consumer. This obligation applies to:

1\) continuous supply of digital content or a digital service during the entire period of time if the content or service must be supplied in accordance with the contract;

2\) supply of one or more digital content or services, for a period of time during which the consumer may reasonably expect, taking into account the type and purpose of the content or service and the circumstances and nature of the contract.

(2) Where a consumer fails to install updates supplied pursuant to subsection 1 of this section within a reasonable time, the trader shall not be liable for non-compliance with the conditions of the contract due to lack of updates if the trader informed the consumer that the updates were available and the consequences of failure to install them, and failure to install the updates or incorrect installation thereof was not due to the shortcomings in the installation instructions provided by the trader.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 01.01.2022\]

##### § 62<sup>9</sup>. Incorrect installation

(1) Non-compliance with the conditions of a contract arising from incorrect installation of digital content or a digital service is deemed to be equal to non-compliance with the conditions of the contract arising from the digital content or digital service if the content or service was installed by or under the responsibility of the trader. The same applies if the digital content or digital service had to be installed by the consumer and the incorrect installation was due to shortcomings in the installation instructions provided by the trader.

(2) Installation is the interconnection and connection of digital content or a digital service to parts of the consumer's digital environment in such a way that the content or service can be used in accordance with the conditions of the contract provided for in this Subchapter.

(3) The digital environment is the hardware, software and network connection used by a consumer to access or use digital content or a digital service.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 01.01.2022\]

##### § 62<sup>10</sup>. Deviating agreements

It is not the case of non-compliance with the conditions of a contract for the purposes of clauses 1–5 of 3 of § 62<sup>7</sup>, subsection 4 of § 62<sup>7</sup> and subsection 1 of § 62<sup>8</sup> of this Act when a consumer was specifically informed at the time of entry into the contract that a particular feature of the digital content or digital service deviates from those sections and the consumer expressly and separately agreed to such deviation at the time of entry into the contract.\
\[RT I, 24.11.2021, 1 – entry into force 01.01.2022\]

##### § 62<sup>11</sup>. Liability of trader for non-compliance of digital content or digital service with conditions of contract
