(2) A commission agent also has the right of security and rights arising therefrom if the commission object belongs to the agent or the agent is the purchaser or seller of the object.

(3) If the principal is declared bankrupt or enforcement proceedings are initiated against the principal, the commission agent has the right to satisfy the claims specified in subsection 1 of this section out of the money received upon performance of the contract of commission before the principal and the obligees thereof.

### Chapter 40 — PAYMENT ORDER AND PAYMENT SERVICE

\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 - entry into force 22.01.2010\]

#### Subchapter 1 — Payment Order

##### § 703. Payment order

(1) With a payment order, the authorised person is ordered to pay or transfer, at the expense of the originator, money or securities to a third party (beneficiary), and the beneficiary is entitled to accept the execution of the order.

(2) A payment order may be given, inter alia, by means of bill of exchange, cheque, credit card or any other similar payment instrument.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

##### § 704. Acceptance of payment order

Acceptance of a payment order is a declaration of intent by which the authorised person accepts the obligation arising from the payment order. The acceptance of a payment order issued in the form of a document shall be entered on the document.

##### § 705. Execution of payment order

(1) The authorised person who has accepted the payment order shall undertake to perform the obligation arising from the payment order and may contest the claim of the beneficiary to execute the payment order only in so far as it arises from the relationship with the beneficiary or from the validity of the payment order or acceptance, and not from the relationship with the originator.

(2) If a payment order is issued in the form of a document, the authorised person shall perform the obligation arising from the payment order only if the document has been delivered to the authorised person.

(3) The authorised person is not required to accept a payment order or perform obligations arising therefrom only because the authorised person is an obligor of the originator. Upon execution of a payment order, the authorised person is however released from the obligations thereof to the extent to which the payment order is executed.

##### § 706. Notification obligation of beneficiary

(1) If a beneficiary learns that the authorised person refuses to accept the payment order or perform the obligation arising therefrom, the beneficiary shall immediately notify the originator thereof.

(2) In the event of a violation of the notification obligation provided in subsection 1 of this section, the originator has the right to demand compensation from the beneficiary for damage caused by the violation of the obligation.

##### § 707. Withdrawal of payment order

Until the authorised person has accepted a payment order or performed the obligation arising therefrom, the originator has the right to withdraw the payment order even if the originator thereby violates the obligations thereof to the beneficiary. In order to withdraw a payment order, the originator shall notify the authorised person thereof.

##### § 708. Restrictions on expiry of payment order

A payment order does not expire upon the death or declaration of bankruptcy of the originator, authorised person or beneficiary.

#### Subchapter 2 — Payment Service Contract

\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 - entry into force 22.01.2010\]

##### Division 1 — General Provisions

###### § 709. Payment service contract and related definitions

(1) Payment service contract means a contract under which, in accordance with law, a mandatary having the right to provide a payment service (hereinafter *payment service provider*) undertakes to make payment transactions specified in the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act by order of the mandator (hereinafter *payer*) and the client of the payment service provider undertakes to pay a fee therefor.

(2) A payment service contract may also be entered into for the execution of a single payment order (hereinafter *single payment service contract*).

(3) A payment service contract may also include the obligation to open a payment account, the conditions for holding thereof and the obligation to provide other payment services.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

(4) Payment account means an account held in the name of the payment service client for the execution of payment transactions.

(5) Payer within the meaning of this Subchapter is a person for whom a payment account has been opened and who gives a payment order for the debiting of the payment account or, if there is no payment account, a person who gives a payment order. Payee within the meaning of this Subchapter is a person who is a beneficiary in conformity with the payment order.

(6) A payment transaction is an act initiated by the payer or on the payer’s behalf or by the payee of placing, transferring or withdrawing funds, irrespective of any legal relationship between the payer and the payee constituting the basis thereof.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

(7) Payment order means any order for the making of a payment transaction which is given by the payer to the payment service provider. A payment order may also be given through the payee.

(8) A payment instrument is any personalised means or set of procedures agreed on between the payment service provider and its client which are used by the client of the payment service provider for the initiation of a payment order.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(8<sup>1</sup>) A card-based payment instrument specified in this Act is a payment instrument within the meaning of Article 2(20) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/751 of the European Parliament and of the Council on interchange fees for card-based payment transactions (OJ L 123, 19.05.2015, pp. 1–15).\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(8<sup>2</sup>) Funds are banknotes and coins, scriptural money or electronic money within the meaning of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(9) A payment service provider may use the help of a payment intermediary upon execution of a payment order. Payment intermediary means a person who participates in making a payment upon agreement with the payment service provider of the payer or the payment service provider of the payee and who is neither the payer nor the payee.

(10) Settlement day is the day on which the payment service provider of the payer or the payment service provider of the payee involved in the execution of a payment transaction, including payment intermediary, is open for business as required for the making of a payment transaction.

(11) Value date means a day when a payment service provider debits the account of the payer or credits the account of the payee and which is the basis for the calculation of interest on the amount of money in the account.

(12) Unique identifier means a combination of letters, numbers or symbols assigned to the client by the payment service provider, which is provided by the client to identify unambiguously the client of the other payment service provider or the payment account thereof used in the payment transaction. The unique identifier may be a payment account number.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

(12<sup>1</sup>) Authentication is an automatic procedure which allows the payment service provider to identify the client or the validity of the use of a specific payment instrument, including the use of personalised security features.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(12<sup>2</sup>) Strong client authentication is the authentication based on the use of at least two security features which function independently and ensure the confidentiality of the authentication data which only the client knows or possesses or which can be attributed only to the client.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(12<sup>3</sup>) A personalised security feature is a component bound to a person and enabling authentication.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(13) \[Repealed – RT I 2010, 77, 590 – entry into force 01.07.2011\]

(14) Reference exchange rate means an exchange rate which is used as the basis to calculate any currency exchange rate and which is made available by the payment service provider or comes from a publicly available source.

(15) Reference interest rate means an interest rate which is used as the basis for calculating any interest rate to be applied and which comes from a publicly available source.

(15<sup>1</sup>) The basic payment services related to payment accounts (hereinafter *basic payment services*) are the following payment services provided to consumers on the basis of payment service contracts:

1\) the payment services which enable consumers to perform all the operations which are required for opening, operating and closing the payment account specified in subsection 4 of this section;

2\) the payment services specified in clause 1 of subsection 1 of § 3 of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act;

3\) the payment services specified in clause 2 of subsection 1 of § 3 of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act which are provided in the European Union at the place of business intended for servicing the customers of credit institutions or automated teller machines or self-service payment terminals during or outside the credit institution's opening hours;\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

4\) the payment service specified in clause 1 of subsection 2 of § 3 of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act within the European Union;\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

5\) the payment service specified in clause 2 of subsection 2 of § 3 of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act, including online payments, within the European Union;\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

6\) the payment service specified in clause 3 of subsection 2 of § 3 of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act, within the European Union, which can be initiated in automated teller machines or self-service payment terminals, places of business intended for servicing the customers of credit institutions or via online facilities.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

(15<sup>2</sup>) Transfer of payment services related to payment accounts (hereinafter *payment service transfer*) is providing, on the basis of the instructions given by a mandate of the consumer, of information about the payment services specified in clauses 1 and 3 of subsection 2 of § 3 of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act, including about receipts on the payment account to another payment service provider or transfer of positive payment account balance of a consumer to a payment account opened at another payment service provider, with or without cancellation of the contract.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

(15<sup>3</sup>) The new payment service provider is the initiator of the payment service transfer to whom the consumer issues a mandate for the payment service transfer and whose former payment service provider sends written information for payment service transfer.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

(15<sup>4</sup>) The former payment service provider is the payment service provider who sends to the new payment service provider the information required for the transfer and performs the acts stipulated in the instructions of the consumer.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

(16) Any settlements at and with *Eesti Pank* are performed on the basis of the *Eesti Pank* Act and legislation arising therefrom.

(17) *Eesti Pank* may establish more detailed requirements on maintenance of payment accounts and settlement of payments by credit institutions and other financial institutions.

(18) This Subchapter also applies to payment transactions executed by means of e-money and contracts related thereto unless otherwise provided in this Subchapter.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2011, 6 – entry into force 18.07.2011\]

(19) This Subchapter does not apply to payment transactions made through payment systems, including the settlement systems specified in the Payment and Settlement Systems Act.\
\[RT I, 01.03.2023, 3 – entry into force 11.03.2023\]

(20) The provisions of this Subchapter do not apply to money transfers where the originator or recipient is a credit institution.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 710. Obligation to ensure access to payment systems

\[Repealed – RT I, 01.03.2023, 3 – entry into force 11.03.2023\]

###### § 710<sup>1</sup>. Obligation to enter into payment service contract and terms and conditions related thereto

(1) If a person and the terms of the contract sought by the person correspond to the provisions of law and the general terms of services or the standard terms of provision of payment service established by the payment service provider, the payment service provider shall, at the request of the person, enter into a payment service contract with the person, under which the payment service provider provides one or several payment services specified in subsection 1 of § 3 of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act to the person in the procedure and to the extent established in the above general terms or standard terms.

(2) Unless otherwise provided in the Act, a credit institution undertakes to provide a consumer, who lawfully resides in the European Union, basic payment services specified in subsection 15<sup>1</sup> of § 709 of this Act and, in the case of justified interest of a consumer, to enter into a payment service contract (hereinafter *basic payment service contract*) to provide the basic payment services. Credit institutions must render the use of basic payment services possible through different channels, including via online facilities.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

(2<sup>1</sup>) Providing proof of sufficient interest must not be unreasonably burdensome for a consumer.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

(3) Credit institutions may not refuse from entry into a basic payment service contract with an alien who holds a valid residence permit or has the right to reside in Estonia as well as with a person enjoying international protection in the meaning of the Act on Granting International Protection to Foreign Nationals due to the nationality or residence of the consumer.

(4) Credit institutions are obliged to, immediately but at the latest within ten settlement days after the receipt of a consumer’s application submitted in compliance with the requirements, enter with the consumer into a basic payment service contract or inform the consumer of refusal to enter into the contract, unless otherwise prescribed in this section.

(5) Credit institutions are obliged to refuse to enter into a basic payment service contract on the grounds provided for in subsection 1 of § 42 of the Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Prevention Act.\
\[RT I, 17.11.2017, 2 – entry into force 27.11.2017\]

(5<sup>1</sup>) A credit institution may not refuse to enter into a basic payment service contract on the basis of the risk appetite determined on the basis of § 10 of the Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Prevention Act, but may implement the following measures in particular to mitigate the risks:

1\) determine the maximum amount of payments made within one month with the funds in the payment account;

2\) determine the maximum amount per one transaction, including a limit for transactions made outside a contracting state of the European Economic Area or from these contracting states;

3\) determine the maximum amount of funds deposited in the payment account;

4\) prohibit or restrict cash withdrawals outside a contracting state of the European Economic Area.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

(5<sup>2</sup>) The measures specified in subsection 5<sup>1</sup> of this section do not apply to transfers of funds in payment of a tax, fine or state fee to an authority.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

(5<sup>3</sup>) The implementation of the measures specified in subsection 5<sup>1</sup> of this section may not be of such a scope or nature as to make it impossible for a consumer to use the basic payment services or as to make it impossible for the consumer and their dependants to meet their living needs.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

(6) Credit institutions are obliged to inform consumers in writing and free of charge of refusal to enter into a basic payment service contract and of the grounds for refusal, unless disclosure of the grounds for refusal is in conflict with the national security of Estonia and public order or the Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Prevention Act.

(7) In the case of refusal to enter into a basic payment service contract, a credit institution is required to give to a consumer the information specified in clauses 23–25 of subsection 1 of § 711 of this Act and disclose the respective contact details.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

(8) A credit institution is not allowed to obligate a consumer, as a prerequisite for entry into a basic payment service contract, to use any additional services or buy shares of the credit institution, unless the latter requirement applies to all consumers.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

(9) Credit institutions are obliged to provide basic payment services to consumers to the same extent compared to other payment services specified in subsection 1 of § 3 of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act.

(9<sup>1</sup>) A credit institution is obliged to provide basic payment services to a consumer at least in euros.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

(10) Credit institutions may not limit the number of transactions related to basic payment services.

(11) Credit institutions must make it possible for consumers use the basic payment services related to a payment account at the places of business intended for servicing the customers of credit institutions and via online facilities, if available.

(12) Credit institutions must provide the following information and terms and conditions free of charge to consumers in their general conditions or standard terms for provision of basic payment services:

1\) persons who are entitled to enter into a basic payment service contract and the terms and conditions of entry into the contract;

2\) fees payable;

3\) the information specified in clauses 23–25 of subsection 1 of § 711 of this Act and the respective contact details;\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

4\) information about that acquisition of additional services shall not constitute a mandatory prerequisite for entry into a basic payment service contract.

(13) Credit institutions are obliged to publish the information and terms and conditions specified in subsection 12 of this section on their website.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

(14) In the case of a dispute, a credit institution provide evidence of non-compliance with the requirements for entry into a basic payment service contract provided in this section.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

###### § 710<sup>2</sup>. Access to payment accounts

(1) Clients are entitled to use payment initiation services and account information services regardless of the mutual agreement between the service provider that provides the payment initiation or account information service and the payment service provider with which the client holds a payment account on provision of the services specified in this subsection.

(2) A payment service provider with which the client holds a payment account may not impose any restrictions or other conditions that treat payment service providers or their clients unequally upon provision of the services specified in subsection 1 of this section, unless imposing of the restrictions is objectively justified or provided by this Act or other legislation.

(3) A payment service provider with which the client holds a payment account may deny a payment service provider that provides payment initiation or account information services access to a payment account for objectively justified reasons, particularly if the access was obtained in an unauthorised or fraudulent manner, including using the payment initiation service upon unauthorised or fraudulent initiation of a payment order. The payment service provider must allow access to the payment account once the reasons for denying access no longer exist.

(4) If possible, the payment service provider shall inform the payer of the circumstances specified in subsection 3 of this section before access to the payment account is denied and immediately after access to the payment account is denied, unless the informing of the payer is not permitted due to security reasons or in other cases provided by law. The payment service provider shall notify the supervisory authority of any circumstances specified in subsection 3 of this section.

(5) The payment service provider with which the client holds a payment account shall allow the client to use, in the case of the services specified in subsection 1 of this section, the authentication method made available to it by the service provider.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

###### § 711. Information concerning payment service contract

(1) A payment service provider shall provide each client with the following information and conditions concerning the terms of the payment service contract:

1\) the name of the payment service provider, the address of its registered office and head office and other relevant address significant in the relations between the client and the payment service provider and, where necessary, the address of its agent or branch if it is situated in Estonia;\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

2\) the name and contact details of the supervisory authority of the payment service provider and a reference to the list specified in § 105 of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act, where the payment service provider is entered;

3\) a description of the payment services provided by the payment service provider;

4\) information or unique identifier to be provided by the client of the payment service provider in order for a payment order to be properly executed;

5\) the form of and procedure for giving consent or approval to execute a payment transaction and for withdrawal of the payment order in accordance with §§ 724<sup>1</sup> and 726 of this Act;

6\) the time of receipt of the payment order in accordance with § 724<sup>2</sup> of this Act;

7\) the maximum term for execution of the payment order;

8\) information concerning a possibility to agree on spending limits on transactions made through the payment instrument in accordance with subsection 2 of § 733<sup>11</sup> of this Act;\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

8<sup>1</sup>) in the case of a co-badged payment instrument, the rights of the client based on Article 8(2) of Regulation (EU) No 2015/751 of the European Parliament and of the Council;\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

9\) the charges payable by a customer of a payment service provider, including any charges relating to the manner and frequency in which the information is provided or made available, and, where applicable, information on the formation of such charges and a breakdown of their amount;\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

10\) where applicable, the interest rates and exchange rates to be applied or, if reference interest rate or exchange rate is to be used, the method of calculating the actual interest, the date and index or the base for determining the reference interest rate or exchange rate;

11\) the manner in and frequency with which information under this Act is provided, and where applicable, the means of distance communication to be used on agreement of the parties, including technical requirements for the means of distance communication of the client of the payment service provider;

12\) information concerning the language or languages, in which communication between the parties is undertaken;

13\) information concerning the right, frequency and manner of receiving information specified in this subsection and in § 727 of this Act;

14\) where applicable, a description of fulfilment of safekeeping requirements of the payment instrument and the manner of notification of the payment service provider in order to fill the requirement under clause 2 of § 733<sup>10 </sup>of this Act;\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

14<sup>1</sup>) procedure for notification of misuse of data relating to provision of the payment service or fraud or potential threat thereof;\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

15\) the conditions on blocking a payment instrument in accordance with subsections 3 and 4 of § 733<sup>11</sup> of this Act;\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

16\) information concerning the liability of the client in accordance with § 733<sup>8</sup> of this Act, which must also include information concerning the amount of the liability limit;

17\) information concerning the notification obligation and the term for its performance in connection with unauthorised payment transactions or incorrectly executed payments in accordance with § 733<sup>7</sup> of this Act;

18\) information concerning the liability of the payment service provider in connection with unexecuted or incorrectly executed payments in accordance with § 733<sup>3</sup> of this Act;

19\) the conditions for refund of the transferred amount in the case of payments initiated by or through a payee in accordance with § 733<sup>6</sup> of this Act;

20\) information concerning the procedure for amendment of the conditions of the payment service contract provided for in § 719<sup>1</sup> of this Act;

21\) duration of the payment service contract;

22\) information concerning the right of the client of the payment service provider to terminate the contract in accordance with § 720 of this Act;

23\) the conditions concerning the law applicable to the payment service contract and the procedure for settlement of disputes;

24\) information concerning the possibility for out-of-court settlement of the disputes and the respective contact details;\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

25\) contact details of the Financial Supervision Authority.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

(2) The information specified in subsection 1 of this section shall be provided to the client of the payment service provider on paper or on another durable medium. The information shall be provided in a clear and unambiguous manner and in Estonian or in another language agreed on by the parties.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

(3) The information shall be considered provided also by the transmission of the draft payment service contract if it includes the information provided for in subsection 1 of this Act.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

(4) A payment service provider is obliged, at any time during the period of validity of the payment service contract at the request of the client of the payment service provider, to provide information concerning the conditions of the payment service contract and other information specified in subsection 1 of this section free of charge.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

(5) The information specified in subsection 1 of this section shall be provided to the client of the payment service provider free of charge in good time before entry into the contract. The payment service provider shall perform the obligation specified in the first sentence of this subsection promptly after entry into the contract if the contract is entered into on the initiative of the client and using such means of distance communication which does not allow the provision of information in accordance with the first sentence of this subsection.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

(6) The provisions on the obligation to provide precontractual information specified in subsection 2 of § 14 and § 14<sup>1</sup> of this Act shall not apply to preparations for entry into a payment service contract.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(7) Payment service providers shall make a consumer rights leaflet prepared by the European Commission and specified in Article 106(1) of Directive 2015/2366/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on payment services in the internal market, amending Directives 2002/65/EC, 2009/110/EC and 2013/36/EU and Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010, and repealing Directive 2007/64/EC available to consumers (OJ L 337, 23.12.2015, pp. 35–127). Payment service providers shall make the leaflet free of charge available in an easily accessible manner on their websites and on paper at the premises of the payment service providers within one month after the publishing of the leaflet.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(8) For clients with disabilities, the leaflet specified in subsection 7 of this section shall be made available if a format which is suitable for the client taking into account the client's disability.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(9) Payment service providers shall ensure that the leaflet specified in subsection 7 of this section shall also be made available to clients by any agents of the payment service provider.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

###### § 711<sup>1</sup>. Information concerning single payment service contract

(1) A payment service provider shall make at least the following information about single payment service contract available to each client:

1\) information or unique identifier to be provided by the client of the payment service provider in order for a payment order to be properly executed;

2\) the maximum term for execution of the payment order;

3\) fees payable by the client of the payment service provider and, where applicable, information concerning the bases for formation of fees or their breakdown;

4\) where applicable, the exchange rate or reference exchange rate used.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

(2) Where applicable, payment service providers shall make any other relevant information specified in subsection 1 of § 711 of this Act and not specified in subsection 1 of this section available in connection with a single payment service contract.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(3) The information specified in this section shall be provided at the request of the client of the payment service provider to the client on paper or on another durable medium before entry into the contract free of charge. The information shall be provided in a clear and unambiguous manner and in Estonian or in another language agreed on by the parties. The provisions of subsection 3 and the second sentence of subsection 5 of § 711 of this Act apply to the provision of information specified in this section.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

(4) Where, on the basis of a single payment service contract, a payment order is given by means of a payment instrument issued on the basis of the payment service contract, the payment service provider has no obligation to provide or make available any information that has already been provided to its client on the basis of the payment service contract entered into with another payment service provider or that will be provided to the client in the future in accordance with this payment service contract.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(5) The provisions on the obligation to provide precontractual information specified in subsection 2 of § 14 and § 14<sup>1</sup> of this Act shall not apply to preparations for entry into a single payment service contract.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2013, 1 – entry into force 13.06.2014\]

(6) Payment service providers providing payment initiation services shall make the following information available to payers before the initiation of the payment:

1\) the name of the payment service provider, the address of its registered office and head office and, where necessary, the address of its agent or branch, if it is situated in Estonia, and its contact details;

2\) the name and contact details of the supervisory authority of the payment service provider.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(7) According to the provisions of subsections 7–9 of § 711 of this Act, payment service providers shall make the consumer rights leaflet specified in subsection 7 of § 711 of this Act available to clients.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(8) Payment service providers that provide account information services shall make the information concerning the conditions of the payment service contract available to clients before provision of the account information service, provided the information is relevant taking into consideration the context of the payment service contract.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(9) Upon provision of the services specified in clause 14 of subsection 1 of § 4 of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act, the information concerning any fees relating to the service and the exchange rates must be made available to clients before and after the provision of the service.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

###### § 711<sup>2</sup>. Charging of fee upon provision of information

(1) A payment service provider may charge a fee for providing or making available information upon agreement of the parties only if the information is requested by the client of the payment service provider and the payment service provider:

1\) provides it, based on an agreement, more frequently than is provided for in §§ 711<sup>1</sup>, 727 and 727<sup>1</sup> of this Act;

2\) provides information, which is not provided for in §§ 711, 711<sup>1</sup>, 727 and 727<sup>1</sup> of this Act; or

3\) provides information in a manner not agreed on in the payment service contract.

(2) A fee for the information provided for in subsection 1 of this section shall be appropriate and in line with the actual costs of the payment service provider.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 711<sup>3</sup>. Information concerning payment services related to payment accounts

(1) Payment service providers must submit to consumers, within a reasonable time period before entry into a payment service contract, a price list (hereinafter price list) based on the list of typical payment services specified in clause 3 of subsection 1 of § 91<sup>1</sup> of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act. Payment service providers must submit the price list to consumers on paper or another durable medium. This does not affect the provisions § 403<sup>1</sup> and 407 and clauses 9, 10 and 20 of subsection 1 of § 711 of this Act.

(2) The price list must:

1\) be a short and stand-alone document;

2\) be presented and laid out in a way that is clear and easy to read, using characters of a readable size;

3\) be no less comprehensible in the event that, having been originally produced in colour, it is printed or photocopied in black and white;

4\) be written in the Estonian language or in another language, if agreed by the consumer;

5\) be accurate and not misleading and stated in the currency of the payment account or, if agreed by the consumer, in any other currency of a state which is a contracting party to the European Economic Area Agreement (hereinafter *contracting party*);

6\) contains the title “List of Typical Payment Services” at the top of the first page next to the common symbol of typical payment service price lists;

7\) state that the price list contains information only about the most typical payment service fees related to payment accounts and that complete information concerning payment service contracts, including pre-contractual information, is submitted in other documents.

(3) Payment service providers prepare and make available to consumers a glossary (hereinafter *glossary*) which is based on the list of typical payment services specified in clause 3 of subsection 1 of § 91<sup>1</sup> of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act. The definitions contained in the glossary must not be misleading and their wording must be clear and unambiguous.

(4) As regards the price list and the glossary, the payment service providers must:

1\) publish them on their website and them available at the places of business intended for servicing their customers;

2\) at the request of a consumer, submit them free of charge on paper or on another durable medium.

(5) Payment service providers must use the definitions of the glossary in the payment service contracts related to payment accounts which are submitted to consumers and in any business and marketing information, if applicable.

(6) Payment service providers may use the symbol of a trade mark for marking the payment service after the definition of the glossary in the payment service contracts related to payment accounts which are submitted to consumers, in any business and marketing information and price list, provided that it is clear which trade mark symbol corresponds to a specific definition in the glossary.

(7) The minister in charge of the policy sector may specify by a regulation the data composition of price lists and the formal requirements thereof.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017 – subsections 1–6 enter into force nine months after entry into force of the implementing regulation of the European Commission specified in Article 3(4) of Directive 2014/92/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on the comparability of fees related to payment accounts, payment account switching and access to payment accounts with basic features (OJ L 257, 28.08.2014, p. 214–246).\]

###### § 711<sup>4</sup>. Limits of fees for basic payment services

(1) If a credit institution charges a fee from consumers for the basic payment services specified in clauses 1–3 and 5 of subsection 15<sup>1</sup> of § 709 of this Act, the fee must be reasonable and the following shall be taken into account upon determination thereof:

1\) the level of income of the residents of Estonia;

2\) the average amount of the fees charged for payment services related to payment accounts by credit institutions in Estonia.

(2) The fees charged for failure to comply with the obligations of consumers arising from basic payment service contracts must be reasonable and determined taking into account the provisions of clauses 1 and 2 of subsection 1 of this section.

(3) The minister in charge of the policy sector may specify by a regulation the bases for determining the fees specified in subsections 1 and 2 of this section.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

###### § 711<sup>5</sup>. Information concerning payment service transfer

(1) Payment service providers shall make the following information available to each consumer concerning the terms and conditions of payment service transfer:

1\) the obligations of the former and new payment service provider specified in §§ 721<sup>1</sup>–721<sup>3</sup> of this Act;

2\) the term for the performance of the respective obligations;

3\) in the case fees are charged, any applicable fees;

4\) the information about what information may be requested from consumers;

5\) the data and terms and conditions specified in clauses 23 and 24 of subsection 1 of § 711 of this Act.

(2) The information specified in subsection 1 of this section must be submitted to consumers free of charge at the place of business intended for servicing of customers and on the website and, at the request of the consumer, on paper or on another durable medium.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

###### § 711<sup>6</sup>. Information concerning services provided together with payment service contract

(1) If a payment service provider offers, together with a payment service contract, an insurance contract or one or more financial services specified in subsection 1 of § 6 of the Credit Institutions Act which are not related to the payment account, the payment service provider must give the following information to the consumers:

1\) whether it is possible to enter separately into a payment service contract;

2\) in the case it is possible to enter into a payment service contract separately, the fees related to each contract or service and the total cost.

(2) If a payment service is provided according to subsection 1 of this section, the payment service provider must submit the following information to the consumer in the price list:

1\) the fees payable for all the services provided in total;

2\) the list of all the services provided;

3\) the volume of the services agreed, including the number of payments and the fee charged from the consumer in the case this number is exceeded.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017 – subsection 2 enters into force nine months after entry into force of the implementing regulation of the European Commission specified in Article 3(4) of Directive 2014/92/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on the comparability of fees related to payment accounts, payment account switching and access to payment accounts with basic features (OJ L 257, 28.08.2014, p. 214–246).\]

###### § 712. \[Repealed – RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 712<sup>1</sup>. Obligations of payment service provider or other account manager provided by law upon provision of financial collateral

(1) Upon encumbrance of funds in an account, including a deposit or another similar financial claim (hereinafter in this section *financial claims*) with financial collateral specified in § 314<sup>1</sup> of the Law of Property Act, a payment service provider or other account manager provided by law is required to maintain records on financial claims in the account such that the financial claims subject to financial collateral are separated from other financial claims held in the account of the pledgor.

(2) A payment service provider or other account manager provided by law is required:

1\) as of the date of entry into force of the irrevocable right to dispose of the financial claims encumbered with financial collateral granted to the pledgee and communicated to the payment service provider, or other account manager provided by law, by the pledgor, to fulfil only the orders of the pledgee to debit the corresponding account with an amount not exceeding the financial claims encumbered with financial collateral;

2\) until the date specified in clause 1 of this subsection, to fulfil the joint orders of the pledgor and pledgee to debit the corresponding account with an amount not exceeding the financial claims encumbered with financial collateral.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

###### § 713. Making of entry in account

(1) The crediting of an account is the making of an entry in the account which increases the obligations of the payment service provider to the client or reduces the obligations of the client to the payment service provider. The account of the client of the payment service provider shall be deemed to be credited if the payment service provider has made a credit entry in the client's account.

(2) The debiting of an account is the making of an entry in the account which reduces the obligations of the payment service provider to the client or increases the obligations of the client to the payment service provider. The account of the client of the payment service provider shall be deemed to be debited if the payment service provider has made a debit entry in the client's account.

(3) A payment service provider may debit the client's account:

1\) on the instruction of the client;

2\) at the request of a third party under the conditions prescribed by the payment service contract;

3\) in other cases provided by law.

(4) A payment service provider may debit the client's account by way of set-off only to set off claims arising from the payment service contract, including to set off the claim for the fee payable to the payment service provider for settlements.

(5) The provisions of subsection 4 of this section do not apply to payment systems, including the settlement systems specified in the Payment and Settlement Systems Act.\
\[RT I, 01.03.2023, 3 – entry into force 11.03.2023\]

###### § 714. Keeping of records by and notification obligation of payment service provider

(1) A payment service provider shall keep records of the crediting and debiting of the client's account.

(2) The client of the payment service provider may, at any time, demand information at the client's expense concerning the balance of the account and details of the crediting or debiting of the account.

(3) A payment service provider shall submit a statement of account to the client at agreed intervals. The payment service provider shall not demand payment from the client for the statement of account specified in this subsection or the forwarding thereof. Unless otherwise agreed, a statement of account concerning a calendar year shall be forwarded by 15 January of the following year at the latest.

(4) On discovering an erroneous entry made in the account, the client shall promptly notify the payment service provider thereof.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 715.

–

###### § 716.

\[Repealed – RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 717. Obligation to pay interest

(1) A payment service provider shall pay interest to the client for the funds deposited in the account of the client of the payment service provider. Interest shall be calculated on an annual basis and interest shall be transferred to the client's account at least once a year.

(2) If the interest rate specified in subsection 1 of this section is not prescribed by the contract, the interest rate shall be that which credit institutions normally pay for demand deposits (call deposits).\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 718. Account maintenance and commission fees

(1) Upon agreement of the parties, account maintenance and commission fees may be demanded from the client. The fee shall be appropriate and in line with the actual costs of the payment service provider.

(2) The provisions of subsection 1 of this section do not apply to securities accounts.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 718<sup>1</sup>. Statement of fees

(1) Payment service providers must give a statement to consumers at least once a year and free of charge of all the fees charged from the consumer for all the payment services included in the list of typical payment services specified in clause 3 of subsection 1 of § 91<sup>1</sup> of the Payment Institutions and E-money Institutions Act (hereinafter *statement of fees*) and, if applicable, of the interest rates specified in §§ 407 and 717 of this Act. This shall not affect the provisions of §§ 407 and 727 of this Act.

(2) Payment service providers must agree with consumers on the means of communication used for sending the statement of fees and, at the request of the consumer, submit it on paper or on another durable medium.

(3) Payment service providers must provide at least the following information in the statement of fees during the respective period:

1\) the cost of each payment service and the number of using the payment service;

2\) the total amount of the fees paid for each payment service;

3\) if applicable, the interest rate of the overdraft agreement and the total amount of interest charged for the use of overdraft;

4\) if applicable, the interest rate paid on the amount of demand deposits and the total amount of the interest earned;

5\) the total amount of fees paid for all the payment services in total.

(4) If payment services are provided according to subsection 1 of § 711<sup>6</sup> of this Act, the payment service provider must state in the statement of fees for the respective period the following information in addition to the provisions of subsection 3 of this section:

1\) the total cost of all the services provided;

2\) how many times the customer was charged the fee based on all the services provided together;

3\) the additional fee charged from the consumer in total for exceeding the agreed volume of services, including exceeding the number of payments.

(5) A statement of fees must:

1\) be presented and laid out in a way that is clear and easy to read, using characters of a readable size for this purpose;

2\) be accurate and not misleading and stated in the currency of the payment account or, if agreed by the consumer and the payment service provider, in the currency of another contracting party;

3\) contain at the top of the first page next to a common symbol of the statement of fees the title “Statement of fees paid for payment services”;

4\) be drawn up in the Estonian language or in another language agreed upon by the consumer and the payment service provider.

(6) Payment service providers may use the symbol of a trade mark for marking the payment services after the definition of the glossary in the statement of fees, provided that it is clear which trade mark symbol corresponds to a specific definition in the glossary.

(7) The minister in charge of the policy sector may specify by a regulation the data composition of statement of fees and the formal requirements thereof.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017, subsections 1–6 enter into force 31.10.2018, nine months after entry into force of the implementing regulation of the European Commission (OJ L 6, 11.01.2018, p. 3–25) specified in Article 3(4) of Directive 2014/92/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on the comparability of fees related to payment accounts, payment account switching and access to payment accounts with basic features (OJ L 257, 28.08.2014, p. 214–246).\]

###### § 719. Duty to maintain confidentiality

(1) A payment service provider and the payment intermediary shall, both during the term of the payment service contract and upon expiry thereof, maintain the confidentiality of all information of which they become aware on the basis of their relationship with the client, including information concerning the client and the account and payment transactions thereof, unless the right or obligation to disclose information arises from legislation.

(2) A payment service provider shall be released from the obligation to maintain confidentiality to the extent that the client has granted consent to the disclosure of information in writing or in a format which can be reproduced in writing.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 719<sup>1</sup>. Amendment of payment service contract

(1) A payment service provider may amend the payment service contract only if the payment service provider notifies the client thereof in the manner provided for in subsection 1 of § 711 of this Act no later than two months before entry into force of the amendment.

(2) A payment service provider and the client may agree that the client consents to amendment of the contract unless the client of the payment service provider notifies the payment service provider of not accepting the amendment before entry into force of the amendment. In such event the payment service provider shall notify the client of the consequences of tacit consent and of the right to cancel the contract in accordance with subsection 3 of this section.

(3) If there is an agreement provided for in subsection 2 of this section between the client of the payment service provider and the payment service provider, the client has the right to cancel the payment service contract promptly and free of charge before entry into force of the amendment.

(4) Upon agreement of the parties, a payment service provider has the right to change the interest rates and exchange rates specified in the payment service contract without prior notice provided that the changes are based on a reference interest rate or reference exchange rate agreed on between the parties.

(5) A payment service provider shall notify the client of any change in the interest rate in the manner provided for in subsection 2 of § 711 of this Act at the earliest opportunity unless otherwise agreed by the parties. There is no obligation to notify the client of changes in the interest rates or exchange rates which are more favourable to the client of the payment service provider.

(6) Changes in the interest rate or exchange rate used shall be implemented and calculated in a manner that enables to treat clients of the payment service provider equally under equal conditions.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 720. Ordinary cancellation of payment service contract

(1) Unless the parties have agreed on the term for advance notice of cancellation, the client of the payment service provider may cancel the payment service contract at any time. Any agreement of the parties whereby a longer term than one month is determined as the term for notice of cancellation is void.

(2) A payment service provider may cancel the payment service contract in the case the contract is entered into for an unspecified term and the parties have agreed on the right to cancel the contract. The term for advance notice of cancellation may not be shorter than two months. An application for cancellation shall be made in the manner provided for in subsection 2 of § 711 of this Act.

(3) In the event of expiry of the payment service contract, the regular fees under the contract are payable only until the expiry of the contract. Upon expiry of the contract, advance payments made by the client of the payment service provider shall be refunded proportionately, considering thereby the actual costs incurred by the payment service provider for the provision of the service by the moment of expiry of the contract.

(4) The client shall not be charged any fee for cancellation of a payment service contract entered into for a term longer than six months or for an unspecified term in the event the client cancels the contract after six months have passed from entry into the contract. In other cases the fees charged shall be appropriate and in line with the costs of termination of the contract.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(5) Upon expiry of a payment service contract, the payment service provider shall pay the funds in the account to the client or a third party designated by the client, or transfer the funds to an account with the same or another payment service provider as specified by the client unless otherwise prescribed by law.

(6) If a payment made to the client is received by the payment service provider within one month as of the expiry of the payment service contract, the payment service provider shall accept the payment, notify the client thereof and pay the amount pursuant to the provisions of subsection 5 of this section.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 720<sup>1</sup>. Cancellation of basic payment service contract

(1) A credit institution may cancel a basic payment service contract only on an extraordinary basis and in the cases provided in this section.

(2) A credit institution cancels a basic payment service contract without notice where:

1\) the ground provided in subsection 1 of § 42 of the Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Prevention Act exists;

2\) the obligation to close the payment account arises from a legal instrument establishing an international or Government of the Republic sanction for the purposes of the International Sanctions Act.

(3) A credit institution may cancel a basic payment service contract entered into with a consumer where:

1\) the consumer has intentionally used the payment account for an unlawful purpose;

2\) the consumer has submitted incorrect information in order to gain access to basic pay services, when they would not have been entitled to do so if they had provided correct information;

3\) the consumer no longer meets the conditions specified in subsection 2 of § 710<sup>1</sup> of this Act;

4\) no transactions have been concluded on the consumer's payment account for at least 24 consecutive months;

5\) the payment account has not had sufficient funds for at least six consecutive months to meet the obligations arising from the basic payment service contract.

(4) On the ground provided in clause 1 of subsection 2 of this section, a credit institution may cancel a basic payment service contract only in the case the risk mitigation measures implemented with respect to the consumer by the credit institution specified in subsection 5<sup>1</sup> of § 710<sup>1</sup> of this Act have been exhausted.

(5) On the grounds provided in clauses 1 and 2 of subsection 3 of this section, a credit institution cancels a basic payment service contract concluded with a consumer without observing the period of advance notice.

(6) In the case of cancellation of a contract on the grounds provided in clauses 3–5 of subsection 3 of this section, the period of advance notice of cancellation may not be less than two months.

(7) A statement of cancellation by a credit institution must be submitted free of charge on a durable medium, in a clear and comprehensible manner, in the Estonian or another language agreed between the parties and it must contain:

1\) reason for the cancellation, unless disclosure thereof is contrary to the national security and public order of Estonia or the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Act;

2\) reference to the law applicable to the payment service contract and the conditions of the dispute settlement procedure;

3\) information on possibilities of out-of-court dispute settlement and respective contact details and contact details of the Financial Supervision Authority.

(8) Where a credit institution cancels a basic payment service contract in accordance with this section, subsections 3, 5 and 6 of § 720 of this Act apply.

(9) Cancellation of a basic payment service contract by a credit institution in a case other than the case specified in subsections 2 and 3 of this section is void.

(10) A cancellation that does not comply with the requirements provided in subsections 6 and 7 of this section is void.

(11) Compliance with the requirements for the cancellation of a basic payment service contract provided in this section is proved by the credit institution in the case of a dispute.\
\[RT I, 08.07.2025, 4 - entry into force 15.07.2025\]

###### § 721. \[Repealed – RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

##### Division 1<sup>1</sup> — Amendment and Termination of Payment Service Contract in connection with Payment Service Transfer

\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 - entry into force 10.01.2017\]

###### § 721<sup>1</sup>. Requirements applicable to domestic payment service transfer

(1) A consumer may give a mandate to a payment service provider specified in subsection 15<sup>3</sup> of § 709 of this Act who has been issued an activity licence or established a branch in Estonia (hereinafter *payment service provider operating in Estonia*) which contains instructions on which terms and conditions all or certain payment services related to a payment account opened in the same currency and specified in clause 15<sup>2</sup> of § 709 of this Act have to be transferred at a payment service provider operating in Estonia.

(2) If two or more persons have the right of claim with respect to a payment account, the new payment service provider must obtain a consent for transfer of the payment service from all the above-mentioned persons.

(3) Consumers must be able to give instructions:

1\) in the Estonian language or other language agreed upon by the consumer and the new payment service provider;

2\) in writing or in a format which can be reproduced in writing or in electronic form and, if necessary, obtain a copy thereof.

(4) Instructions of consumers must contain:

1\) the payment services which the consumer wishes to transfer;

2\) the date from which the new payment service provider must execute standing orders and direct debit orders whereas the specified date cannot be earlier than six settlement days after receipt of the data specified in clause 1 of subsection 1 of § 721<sup>3</sup> of this Act from the former payment service provider.

(5) Consumers give instructions by a mandate to the new payment service provider for execution of the act specified in § 721<sup>2</sup> of this Act.

(6) In the case of payment service transfer, a payment service provider operating in Estonia is not required to provide such services to the consumer which are not provided by the payment service provider.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

###### § 721<sup>2</sup>. Obligations on new payment service provider

(1) Where the instructions of a consumer so prescribe, the new payment service provider must submit, within two settlement days after receipt of the mandate specified in subsection 1 of § 721<sup>1</sup> of this Act, a request to the former payment service provider for obtaining the following information and execution of the following acts:

1\) list of the transferred standing order contracts and all the information it has concerning direct debit contracts in force;

2\) all the information it has concerning the credit orders received in the payment account of the consumer and the direct debit orders debited from the consumer’s payment account during the last 13 months;

3\) termination of execution of standing orders from the date specified in the consumer’s instructions;

4\) transfer of the positive balance of the consumer’s payment account to the payment account of the consumer opened with the new payment service provider on the date specified in the instructions of the consumer;

5\) termination of payment service contract from the date specified in the consumer’s instructions.

(2) If the former payment service provider is unable to automatically redirect received credit and direct debit orders, the new payment service provider has the right to request from the former payment service provider termination of execution of credit and direct debit orders from the date specified in the instructions of the consumer.

(3) At the request of a consumer, the new payment service provider is required to submit a list to the consumer of the payment services specified in clause 1 of subsection 1 of this section and the existing information concerning the payment services specified in subsection 2 of this section which are transferred.

(4) If so prescribed in the instructions of a consumer, the new payment service provider must execute the following acts within five settlement days after receipt of the information specified in clauses 1 and 2 of subsection 1 of this section:

1\) to enter into a contract with the consumer for execution of standing orders and perform it from the date specified in the instructions of the consumer;

2\) to enter into a contract with the consumer for execution of direct debit orders and perform it from the date specified in the instructions of the consumer;

3\) to send to the payers specified in the instructions of the consumer the details of the payment account of the consumer and a copy of the instructions of the consumer;

4\) to send to the payees specified in the instructions of the consumer the details of the payment account of the consumer and the date for debiting the payment account on the basis of direct debit orders and a copy of the instructions of the consumer.

(5) Payment service providers ensure upon sending a copy of the consumer’s instructions specified in clauses 3 and 4 of subsection 4 of this section that the information is disclosed to the payer or payee only with regard to the payment services related to them.

(6) If the new payment service provider does not have the information to be sent to the payers specified in clause 3 and payees specified in clause 4 of subsection 4 of this section, the new payment service provider must request the missing information from the consumer or former payment service provider.

(7) If a consumer decides to personally send the information specified in clauses 3 and 4 of subsection 4 of this section to payers or payees, the new payment service provider must send, within five settlement days after receipt of the information specified in clauses 1 and 2 of subsection 1 of this section, a standard letter to the consumer which contains the details of the payment account of the consumer and the beginning date of the direct debit orders specified in the instructions of the consumer (hereinafter *consumer's details*). In this case, the new payment service provider is not required to inform the payers or payees of the details of the specified consumer.

(8) Where appropriate, the new payment service provider is obliged to inform the consumer according to the requirements for sending information provided for in subsections 1–3 of § 711 of this Act and during the term specified in subsection 4 of this section of the rights of the consumer specified in Article 5(3)(d) of the Regulation (EU) of the European Parliament and of the Council No 260/2012 establishing technical and business requirements for credit transfers and direct debits in euro and amending Regulation (EC) No 924/2009 (OJ L 94, 30.03.2012, pp. 22–37) to demand the following from the payment service provider:

1\) execution of direct debit orders must be based on the amounts specified in the instructions of the consumer or frequency or both;

2\) if the consumer does not have the right to a refund specified in § 733<sup>6</sup> of this Act, the consumer must check upon filling in the direct debit order before debiting of the payment account of the consumer whether the amount and frequency correspond to the amount and frequency specified in the instructions of the consumer;

3\) blocking of execution of direct debit orders.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

###### § 721<sup>3</sup>. Obligations on former payment service provider

(1) A former payment service provider must, after submission of a request by the new payment service provider and if so prescribed in the instructions of the consumer, perform the following acts based on subsections 1 and 2 of § 721<sup>2</sup> of this Act:

1\) to send to the new payment service provider the data specified in clauses 1 and 2 of subsection 1 of § 721<sup>2</sup> of this Act within five settlement days after submission of the request of the new payment service provider;

2\) to terminate the execution of direct debit orders from the date specified in the instructions of the consumer;

3\) to transfer the positive balance of the payment account of the to the payment account opened with the new payment service provider on the date specified in the instructions of the consumer.

(2) Unless this is contrary to the provisions of subsection 1 of § 720 of this Act and no unfulfilled obligations or other obligations which are not yet due are related to the consumer’s payment account and the acts specified in subsection 1 of this section have been completed, the former payment service provider must terminate the consumer’s payment service contract from the date specified in the instructions of the consumer. The former payment service provider is obliged to immediately inform the consumer of such obligations which hinder termination of the payment service contract.

(3) If the former payment service provider is unable to automatically redirect the credit and received direct debit orders specified in subsection 2 of § 721<sup>2</sup> of this Act, the former payment service provider must terminate the performance of the credit and direct debit orders from the date specified in the instructions of the consumer.

(4) At least within one month after closing of a payment account, the former payment service provider shall send information about closure of the payment account to the payers or payees in the case of whom the payment transactions initiated by them are not accepted due to closure of the payment account.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

(5) To avoid interruption of payment service upon transfer thereof, the former payment service provider must not block any payment instruments before the date indicated in the instructions of the consumer, unless this is contrary to the provisions of subsection 3 of § 733<sup>11</sup> of this Act.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

###### § 721<sup>4</sup>. Requirements applicable to cross-border payment service transfer

(1) If a consumer has submitted a request to a payment service provider operating in Estonia to transfer all the payment services specified in subsection 15<sup>2</sup> of § 709 of this Act to a payment service provider located in another contracting party and if so prescribed in the request of the consumer, the payment service provider operating in Estonia must assist the consumer make the following acts:

1\) to submit a list to the consumer free of charge of the standing order contracts transferred and all the information it has concerning the direct debit contracts in force;

2\) to submit to the consumer free of charge all the information it has concerning the credit orders received in the payment account of the consumer and the direct debit orders debited from the consumer’s payment account during the last 13 months;

3\) provided that the consumer has indicated in his or her request the details of the consumer’s new payment account and the new payment service provider, to transfer the positive balance of the consumer’s payment account to the consumer’s payment account opened at a payment service provider in another contracting party;

4\) to terminate the payment service contract.

(2) Unless this is contrary to the provisions of subsection 1 of § 720 of this Act and the payment account of the consumer is not burdened with any unfulfilled obligations, the payment service provider operating in Estonia must:

1\) complete the acts specified in subsection 1 of this section by the date specified in the request of the consumer but not earlier than six settlement days after receipt of the request of the consumer, unless the consumer and the payment service provider have agreed otherwise;

2\) notify the consumer immediately of such obligations or restrictions which hinder termination of the payment service contract, unless otherwise provided for in the legislation.

(3) A payment service provider operating in Estonia is not required to provide such services to a consumer arriving from another contracting party which are not included among the services provided by it.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

###### § 721<sup>5</sup>. Limits of fees for transfer of payment services

(1) Consumers shall not be charged for submission of the list specified in clause 1 of subsection 1 of § 721<sup>2</sup> of this Act of consumer’s standing and direct debit orders in force and the information specified in subsection 2 of the same section.

(2) Former payment service providers may not charge a fee from the new payment service provider for submission of the list specified clause 1 of subsection 1 of § 721<sup>2</sup> of this Act and the information specified in subsection 2 of this section.

(3) Former payment service providers must proceed upon determination of fees in the case of termination of payment service contracts of a consumer from the provisions of subsections 3 and 4 of § 720 of this Act.

(4) The fee for any services specified in §§ 721<sup>1</sup>–721<sup>3</sup> of this Act must be relevant and correspond to the actual costs of the payment service provider.\
\[RT I, 31.12.2016, 1 – entry into force 10.01.2017\]

##### Division 2 — Performance of Payment Service Contract

\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 - entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 722.

–

###### § 724.

\[Repealed – RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 724<sup>1</sup>. Authorisation of payment

(1) A payment transaction is binding to the payer if the payer has given consent to its execution (hereinafter *authorisation*). Consent may be given before execution of the transaction or upon agreement of the parties also by means of retroactive approval.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

(2) The manner and procedure of authorisation for the execution of one or several payment transactions shall be determined upon agreement of the parties. If consent is given to execution of a payment transaction in a manner not agreed on, the execution of the payment transaction is not deemed to be authorised.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

(3) A payer may give consent to execution of a payment transaction using a payment instrument agreed on between the payer and the payment service provider, likewise through the payee or in the case of the payment initiation service through the payment service provider that provides the payment initiation service.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

###### § 724<sup>2</sup>. Receipt of payment order

(1) A payment order is binding to a payment service provider from the moment the payment service provider receives it.

(2) If a payment service provider receives a payment order on a day which is not a settlement day of the payment service provider, the payment order is deemed received on the settlement day following such day.

(3) A payment service provider may determine that a payment order which is received before the end of a settlement day, but after a determined time, is deemed received on the following settlement day. The determined time shall not significantly differ from the time of end of the settlement day.

(4) If a client of the payment service provider who initiates a payment order or by whom or through whom a payment order is initiated and the payment service provider agree on the exact time for execution of the payment order, the payment order is deemed received at the agreed time for the purposes of the provisions of § 728 of this Act. If the agreed time falls on a day which is not a settlement day of the payment service provider, the payment order is deemed received on the settlement day following such day.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 724<sup>3</sup>. Refusal to execute payment order

(1) If a payment service provider refuses to execute a payment order, it shall notify the client who has initiated the payment order thereof and, if possible, of reasons therefor and of possibilities for correcting the payment order. A payment service provider is not required to provide the reasons for refusal if the payment service provider would thereby violate an obligation imposed on it by other legislation.

(2) The notice specified in subsection 1 of this section shall be provided or made available in the manner agreed on by the parties promptly or no later than within the time limits established in § 728 of this Act.

(3) A payment service contract may include a condition according to which a fee must be paid to the payment service provider for the notification specified in subsection 1 of this section if refusal to execute the payment order is justified.

(4) A payment service provider has no right to refuse to execute an authorised payment order if the payment order meets the conditions determined in the payment service contract and the execution of the payment order does not violate any obligation established by other legislation.

(5) A payment order which execution has been justifiably refused is considered as a not received payment order in accordance with the provisions of §§ 728 and 733<sup>3</sup> of this Act.\
\[RT I 2010, 2, 3 – entry into force 22.01.2010\]

###### § 724<sup>4</sup>. Confirmation and limitation of funds

(1) A payment service provider shall, upon the request of a payment service provider issuing card-based payment instruments, immediately confirm whether an amount necessary for the execution of a payment transaction is available on the payment account of the payer, provided that the following conditions are met:

1\) confirmation of availability of the necessary amount of money is requested by the payment service provider who has issued the card-based payment instrument which is used for the transaction;

2\) at the time of the request, the payment account of the payer is accessible via an online connection;

3\) the request was submitted for the exact payment amount of the payment transaction;

4\) the request was submitted for execution of a payment transaction by card-based payment instruments, except for payment instruments on which the electronic money is stored;

5\) the payer has given an explicit consent for confirmation of the availability of the necessary amount of money.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(2) A payment service provider shall submit the request specified in subsection 1 of this section only with the express consent of the payer.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(3) The confirmation of a payment service provider of the availability of the amount of money in the payment account of the payer which is necessary for execution of the payment transaction may not include any other information, including information on the account balance or account statement.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(4) A payment service provider may not block or otherwise restrict the use of the funds in the payment account of the payer on the basis of the request specified in subsection 1 of this section.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 13.01.2018\]

(5) The payment service provider with which the payer holds a payment account shall submit, upon the request of the payer, the identification code of the payment service provider that issued the card-based payment instrument and a confirmation of the availability of the necessary amount of money even to the payer.\
\[RT I, 07.12.2017, 1 – entry into force 14.09.2019, i.e. 18 months after the entry into force of the Commission Implementing Regulation specified in Article 98 of Directive 2015/2366/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on payment services in the internal market, amending Directives 2002/65/EC, 2009/110/EC and 2013/36/EU and Regulation (EU) No 1093/2010, and repealing Directive 2007/64/EC (OJ L 337, 23.12.2015, pp. 35–127).
